items.title: Reported Death of Uyghur Woman Detained Since Age 14
items.description: The girl in the picture looking straight into the camera with probing eyes is 15-year-old Rahile Omer. She was photographed in March 2018 among hundreds of other detainees at a political re-education camp in Konasheher county, Kashgar, Xinjiang. A 2022 BBC investigation identified her as the youngest among the hundreds whose headshots were leaked in the Xinjiang Police Files. Previous records show authorities detained her at age 14 shortly after her parents’ detention in mid-2017. Click to expand Image Then-15-year-old Rahile Omer photographed at a political re-education camp in Kashgar, in China’s Xinjiang region, March 2018. © Victims of Communism Memorial Foundation On November 6, Radio Free Asia (RFA) reported that Rahile, at 23, had died in Peyazawat women’s prison while serving an unjust 12-year sentence. Human Rights Watch has not been able to independently verify this information, but the report should raise alarm about what is happening to the countless Uyghurs who remain behind bars as part of the Chinese government’s crimes against humanity since 2016. Authorities sentenced her in 2021, when she turned 18, reportedly for “disturbing social order,” according to RFA. Chinese officials familiar with her situation told RFA that she was transferred to prison because she did not provide information about others and was caught praying at the dormitory during her “re-education.” They said she possibly died of a heart problem. Hundreds of Uyghurs in the diaspora are mourning Rahile. As a member of this community, I fear receiving similar heartbreaking news every day. My father, Memet Yaqup, is serving a 16-year prison sentence; my uncle, Emet Yaqup, is serving life. I do not know their exact locations or the charges against them, nor do I know if they are still alive. The last time I got word about them was in 2024, when a source told me, “You should be thankful that your father and uncle are still alive, we have lost many lives over the years.” Global attention has led Beijing to strictly control information from Xinjiang. Authorities deny independent observers, including United Nations human rights experts, unfettered access to the region while organizing carefully choreographed official tours for select friendly diplomats, journalists, social media influencers, and members of the Uyghur diaspora to present a sense of normalcy to the outside world. Rahile Omer punctuates this narrative, and governments should press Beijing to answer the question: What happened to her?

items.title: Anambra to prioritise erosion control in environmentally responsible communities
items.description: By Vincent Ujumadu The Anambra State Government has resolved to prioritise communities that demonstrate environmental responsibility in its interventions to control erosion across the state. The decision was taken at the weekly State Executive Council (EXCO) meeting in Awka, where the government said communities engaging in practices that worsen erosion would no longer receive priority attention. The prohibited practices include sand excavation, indiscriminate felling of trees, deforestation, dumping of refuse in drainage channels and directing stormwater onto roads. The State Commissioner for Information and Value Reformation, Dr Law Mefor, who disclosed this after the meeting, said perpetrators of such practices would also be prosecuted to serve as a deterrent to others. Anambra has more than 1,000 active erosion sites affecting communities across the state, with experts arguing that addressing the scale of the problem would require federal and international intervention. Also at the meeting, the EXCO directed that Ogbodi in Amichi community, Nnewi South Local Government Area, which was recently cut off by gully erosion, should be reconnected within two weeks through palliative measures. Mefor said the process of identifying a permanent solution to the erosion problem would commence immediately. The erosion had cut off Ogbodi residents from other parts of Amichi, disrupting access and movement within the community. Meanwhile, the State EXCO approved what it described as the “Soludozie Anambra Framework”, an organised and inclusive platform designed to promote development through the Public-Private-Community Partnership (PPCP) model. According to Mefor, the initiative is intended to provide a structured channel through which Anambra indigenes at home and in the diaspora, as well as other well-meaning individuals, can partner with the state government to drive development. He explained that under the framework, the government’s role would generally be limited to documentation, recognition and support where requested, while donors and partners would directly manage their funds and projects. Mefor said the initiative was aimed at positioning Anambra as a model of collective governance and inclusive development, while accelerating the state’s development. The post Anambra to prioritise erosion control in environmentally responsible communities appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Nvidia’s CEO probe and Singapore ties: Will future chip orders suffer?
items.description: SINGAPORE: Nvidia, which is powering the global artificial intelligence revolution with the chips it makes, is investigating if its chief executive officer, Jensen Huang, was the target of foreign spying. This comes after media reports in October alleged that the Taiwan-born technology maverick had a close relationship with a Chinese businesswoman who passed information to Beijing. The woman, Alice Huang, is a former executive of Singapore-based cloud computing firm Megaspeed International. She is reportedly being monitored by the United States authorities, which suspects she was helping China evade limits on its ability to access advanced AI chips. Singapore has traditionally been among Nvidia’s top four markets in billable revenue. How close are Nvidia’s ties to Singapore? The Straits Times answers this and more. How important is Singapore to Nvidia’s business? Nvidia’s financial reports over the past three years revealed that Singapore was among its top global markets by revenue. But no Singapore revenue breakdown has been given since the middle of 2025. Singapore accounted for 22 per cent of Nvidia’s total revenue at close to US$10.2 billion for the quarter that ended on July 27, 2025. It was the most recent and last known quarterly revenue breakdown for Singapore. The US is Nvidia’s largest market, accounting for about 50pc of total revenue at around US$23.5 billion in that quarter. In the financial year that ended on Jan 26, 2025, Singapore was also the No. 2 contributor to Nvidia’s total revenue, accounting for 18pc of it at nearly US$23.7 billion. The US contributed 47pc of total revenue at almost US$61.3 billion. Why is a small country like Singapore buying so many AI chips? Nvidia had explained that customers used Singapore to “centralise invoicing”, while its products were almost always shipped elsewhere. For instance, for the quarter that ended on July 27, 2025, over 99pc of Nvidia’s revenue billed to Singapore from selling export-controlled data centre products, including AI chips, was for orders from US-based customers. Earlier in January 2025, it was reported that the US was investigating if Chinese AI firm DeepSeek got Nvidia AI chips through countries such as Singapore. In February 2025, the then-Ministry of Trade and Industry responded to these allegations, citing Nvidia as saying many of its customers “use their business entities in Singapore to purchase chips for products destined for the US and other Western countries”. “We expect US companies, like Nvidia, to comply with US export controls and our domestic legislation,” the ministry said, adding that Singapore would act decisively and firmly against individuals and companies that flout the rules. Nvidia had also stated that there was no reason to believe that DeepSeek obtained any export-controlled products from Singapore. In October 2025, it was reported that the US was investigating whether Singapore’s Megaspeed was involved in helping Chinese tech firms sidestep US export controls to obtain restricted Nvidia AI chips. What ties and partnerships does Nvidia have in Singapore? Nvidia has many business and research dealings with organisations in Singapore. In March 2026, Singtel unit NCS said it was integrating NCS’ AI platforms with Nvidia’s AI enterprise software so highly regulated organisations can deploy AI agents — bots which can take actions with minimal human supervision — with the necessary safeguards. These include ensuring that sensitive operational data is protected. The US tech firm said in September 2026 that Sea — which owns e-commerce platform Shopee, financial services arm Monee and gaming platform Garena — was adopting an Nvidia platform to scale the use of AI across its platforms. Sea has used AI to let sellers create product listings, boost fraud detection and build in-game companions that respond to players in real time. The US tech giant has tie-ups with the Singapore Government as well. In September, Singapore’s Home Team Science and Technology Agency (HTX) said it was the first organisation in the country to deploy Nvidia’s latest GB300 chip. The GB300 chips provide massive computing power so HTX can train much smarter AI to process text, video and audio at once and control robots at scale without fear of security being compromised. This builds on HTX’s earlier partnership with Nvidia. Many institutes of higher learning here work with Nvidia on research. In March 2026, the Singapore University of Technology and Design worked with Nvidia and other partners to show how robots and autonomous vehicles can distribute their “thinking” across the device and the cloud. The Singapore Institute of Technology (SIT) and Nvidia jointly established in 2024 a research centre called the SIT x Nvidia AI Centre that has allowed businesses from manufacturing and transport to healthcare sectors develop and test solutions using AI. The centre also launched a new training initiative in October 2025 to help fresh graduates and mid-career professionals become AI practitioners. How will current or future chip orders from Singapore be affected? The outlook is unclear. Taiwan’s Commercial Times cited supply chain rumours suggesting that Nvidia has plans to slow chip orders. It is not clear if this is linked to the ongoing probe into its chief. Reuters reported analysts as saying that a prolonged investigation could delay Nvidia’s investment decisions or product launches, affecting the broader semiconductor industry. In the near term, Nvidia’s competitors like Advanced Micro Devices could gain attention, Ryu Young-ho, a senior analyst at NH Investment & Securities, told Reuters . But replacing Nvidia’s products would be tough, he said. What are Nvidia’s ties to Megaspeed? Megaspeed is under probe in Singapore and the US over possible breaches of export laws involving advanced Nvidia AI chips. It was first incorporated in 2015 as 7Road International, a Chinese gaming company with ties to state-backed investors. Records from the Accounting and Corporate Regulatory Authority show that Megaspeed is still operating at its Collyer Quay office. In February 2024, it incorporated Speedmatrix with two addresses in Johor and Singaporean Tan Yong Pong as its director. According to The New York Times , Speedmatrix was used to receive shipments of Nvidia chips from the US. Tan became Megaspeed’s director in November 2023, shortly after he incorporated Swiftdata, which owns Megaspeed. When 7Road was renamed Megaspeed in March 2023, it was owned by Huang Le Limited and led by Huang Le, who also goes by the name Alice. The ownership was later transferred to Tan’s Swiftdata in November 2023. Alice was seen at the Computex 2024 party in Taipei, where Nvidia’s chief met his top clients. The two Huangs are not related despite sharing the same surname. On Oct 29, The New York Times reported that Alice, a Chinese citizen, was recruited by Beijing to collect intelligence on the Nvidia chief. He later admitted in a message to employees that he had been unfaithful to his wife and took “full responsibility” for his actions. Nvidia said its CEO was committed to continuing to lead the company without interruption. Is Megaspeed being investigated by the Singapore authorities? The Singapore Police Force told The Wall Street Journal on Oct 30 that Megaspeed is being investigated and that it was unable to comment further on the case for now. The police said that while Singapore does not implement unilateral export controls imposed by foreign jurisdictions, the country “does not condone businesses deliberately using their association with Singapore to circumvent or violate other countries’ export controls”. The police added that firm action would be taken against those engaged in fraudulent and dishonest practices. Singapore has charged four people and four companies in court between February 2025 and July 2026 for committing fraud on suppliers of servers, the police added. They face charges that carry jail terms of up to 20 years each. The Wall Street Journal ’s report then cited sources that Singapore officials were concerned with Alice’s close ties to the Nvidia chief, or her being an alleged Chinese intelligence source, and had separately investigated her ties to China. Singapore’s Ministry of Home Affairs clarified on Oct 31 that neither the Singapore Government nor its officials had said that, adding that “there were no such investigations conducted in respect of Alice Huang”.

items.title: Tinubu to Jigawa people: We’ll take this work further to 2031
items.description: President Bola Tinubu has expressed confidence in extending his administration’s development agenda beyond 2027, telling the people of Jigawa State that his government would take its work further “all the way to 2031”. Tinubu made the declaration in a post on his X platform on Wednesday, following his visit to Dutse, the Jigawa State capital, where he commissioned agricultural equipment, skills centres and road projects. The President expressed appreciation to the people of the state for the warm reception accorded him and Vice President Kashim Shettima, saying the visit was a special one. “Jigawa! Nagode sosai! “I am still smiling from Dutse. You welcomed Vice President Shettima and I like family, and you even got your President dancing! Today was special,” he wrote. Tinubu said the commissioning of 400 tractors and 60 combine harvesters was aimed at improving agricultural productivity, increasing farmers’ incomes and strengthening food security. He said the equipment would help farmers produce more food, earn higher incomes and improve the economic wellbeing of their families and communities. The President also highlighted the skills centres established in the state, saying they were already providing young people with opportunities to acquire various vocational skills. He added that improved road infrastructure was opening up more markets for farmers and traders. According to him, the All Progressives Congress (APC) administration’s vision of shared prosperity is anchored on improving farmers’ earnings, creating opportunities for young people and ensuring more families benefit from Nigeria’s progress. Tinubu commended Governor Umar Namadi for his partnership and service to the people of Jigawa State. He also thanked residents for their support, prayers and hospitality, saying he would return to Abuja with fond memories of the visit. “Together, we will take this work further, all the way to 2031!” the President added. The post Tinubu to Jigawa people: We’ll take this work further to 2031 appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: SERAP demands Ojukwu’s release, end to prosecution of journalists
items.description: The Socio-Economic Rights and Accountability Project (SERAP) has called on President Bola Tinubu and the Attorney-General of the Federation, Lateef Fagbemi, SAN, to secure the immediate release of Daniel Ojukwu, a journalist with the Foundation for Investigative Journalism (FIJ), from the Kuje Correctional Centre, Abuja. The organisation also urged the Federal Government to end the use of criminal defamation and cyberstalking charges to intimidate or punish journalists for reporting on alleged corruption and the management of public funds. SERAP made the demands following the remand of Ojukwu at the Kuje Correctional Centre by Justice Joyce Abdulmalik of the Federal High Court, Abuja, pending the determination of his bail application. Ojukwu was reportedly remanded on Tuesday until December 1, 2026, after being arraigned on 12 counts bordering on alleged cyberstalking and criminal defamation. He pleaded not guilty to all the charges. The court subsequently adjourned the hearing of his pending bail application until December. SERAP also called for an end to the prosecution and alleged harassment of Ojukwu and FIJ founder, Fisayo Soyombo, over investigative reports concerning alleged expenditure of public funds by the Office of the Senior Special Assistant to the President on Sustainable Development Goals (OSSAP-SDGs). The organisation expressed concern that Ojukwu’s detention could send a chilling message to journalists and others seeking to expose alleged corruption and scrutinise the management of public resources. It said the prosecution stemmed from investigative reports published in 2023 and January 2024, which raised questions about payments of N147.1 million and N47.5 million for classroom construction projects, as well as reports that solar panels installed at some of the projects stopped functioning shortly after their completion. Describing the issues raised in the reports as matters of legitimate public interest, SERAP said public officials and institutions should expect scrutiny of their decisions and expenditure of public funds. It argued that the appropriate response to investigative reports questioning public expenditure was for authorities to provide explanations, disclose relevant records and, where necessary, investigate allegations of wrongdoing rather than prosecute and imprison journalists. The organisation further described Ojukwu’s latest detention as particularly troubling, recalling that he was previously detained for 10 days in May 2024 over reporting concerning the same public official and alleged expenditure of public funds. It warned that his continued prosecution could reinforce an atmosphere in which journalists are discouraged from investigating and reporting on corruption for fear of arrest, detention and imprisonment. SERAP cited Sections 22 and 39 of the 1999 Constitution, as amended, Article 9 of the African Charter on Human and Peoples’ Rights and Article 19 of the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights, noting that they guarantee freedom of expression and media freedom. It said the protections include the right to seek, receive and impart information and ideas, including views that may be critical, controversial or unwelcome to public officials. According to the organisation, freedom of expression is particularly important when journalists report on alleged corruption, public expenditure and the conduct of people entrusted with public responsibilities. It maintained that public officials must tolerate robust scrutiny and criticism, particularly concerning the exercise of public power and management of public resources. SERAP also referred to paragraph 47 of the United Nations Human Rights Committee’s General Comment No. 34, which cautions against the use of defamation laws to stifle freedom of expression. The committee, it noted, urges states to recognise truth and public interest as defences, avoid excessively punitive measures and consider decriminalising defamation. items.title: Une Sidwaya du 11-11-2026
Dollar to Naira exchange rate today, November 11, 2026
items.description: The US dollar is trading at approximately ₦1,350 per dollar at the Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market (NFEM), while the naira exchanges at between ₦1,411 and ₦1,419 per dollar in the parallel market on Wednesday, November 11, 2026. Available exchange rate reports indicate that the official market rate was around ₦1,350.36 per dollar on Tuesday, November 10, while parallel-market dealers quoted buying and selling rates of approximately ₦1,411 and ₦1,419, respectively. At the parallel market, also known as the black market, the exchange rate varies depending on the location and the Bureau De Change (BDC) operator. The latest reported parallel-market figures indicate that Nigerians selling $1 to currency dealers could receive approximately ₦1,411, while those purchasing $1 may pay about ₦1,419. At the official market, the NFEM rate remains the benchmark for foreign exchange transactions in Nigeria. The difference between the reported official rate of ₦1,350.36 and the parallel market selling rate of ₦1,419 is approximately ₦68.64 per dollar. The exchange rate may change during the day depending on dollar supply, demand and trading activities across the foreign exchange market. Nigerians are advised to confirm prevailing rates with their banks and licensed currency dealers before carrying out foreign exchange transactions. items.title: PTI founder Imran Khan brought to Pims, undergoes eye procedure
items.description: ISLAMABAD: Former prime minister and PTI founder Imran Khan was again taken to the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (Pims) for tests and follow-up treatment for his eye condition, a hospital official told Dawn on Wednesday. “Imran Khan was brought from the Adiala jail in Rawalpindi to Pims in Islamabad during the night between Nov 10 and 11 for a medical check-up and follow-up eye treatment on the advice of the ophthalmologist treating him,” the official said. The hospital official added that, prior to the procedure, the former premier underwent a medical examination, including an ocular assessment. “His vital parameters were found to be normal. He was clinically stable, and his general physical examination was unremarkable. After obtaining informed consent and following standard monitoring procedures, precautionary measures and clinical protocols, the ophthalmology team administered an intravitreal anti-VEGF injection,” the official said. He added that Imran remained “clinically stable before, during and after the procedure”. The PTI founder was discharged at around 2:30am with the necessary instructions for further care and follow-up, according to the official. The former premier’s last reported hospital visit to Pims for his eye ailment was in June. Imran has been imprisoned since August 2023, and his health has deteriorated over the course of his prison sentence, prompting outcry from members of the party. His eye ailment — right central retinal vein occlusion — came to light in late January, following which he has been taken to hospital multiple times. On Aug 18, the Supreme Court directed the government to shift the jailed ex-premier to Shifa International Hospital in Islamabad, a day after the superintendent of the Adiala jail — where Imran is imprisoned — submitted a report to the SC on the ex-premier’s health condition. In the report, the jail administration said adequate healthcare facilities were being provided to Imran and his wife, with their health and well-being a priority. However, an annexure to the report stated that Dr Akhtar Ali Bandeshah of Pims examined him on Aug 1 and noted complaints of uncontrolled and fluctuating blood pressure, palpitations, headache and restlessness. The ex-premier had attributed his symptoms and stress partly to infrequent meetings with his wife, family and social contacts, as well as the absence of newspapers and TV. On Aug 10, the SC was informed, a medical board comprising Pims specialists also examined Imran after he complained of heaviness in the head and palpitations. It recommended a one-hour daily walk and relaxation in his prison routine, besides access to newspapers, magazines, television and books. The board also recommended more frequent interaction with immediate family members or his spouse, saying this could help control his anxiety and blood pressure. Subsequently, the court ordered his transfer to Shifa International Hospital. However, the government took the PTI founder to Pims and subsequently transported him back to prison. At the time, Information Minister Attaullah Tarar had blamed “the security situation created by PTI workers on the way to and outside” the hospital for the diversion. The PTI has denied the allegations and accused the government of deliberately flouting the court’s orders.

items.title: Ebola cases in DR Congo pass 11,000, with 5,387 deaths
items.description: The number of confirmed Ebola cases in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) has reached 11,042, according to government data, with at least 5,387 deaths. The figures, released on Tuesday, came as health authorities in the DRC struggle to contain the largest and deadliest Ebola outbreak in the country’s history. The outbreak is caused by the rare Bundibugyo strain of the Ebola virus. It is now the second-largest and second-deadliest Ebola outbreak on record, behind only the 2014-2016 West African outbreak. That epidemic infected more than 28,600 people and killed more than 11,000. Eight of the DRC’s 26 provinces have been affected in the ongoing outbreak, and many deaths have occurred outside treatment centres. Delayed detection, conflict and strained health services have led to a more rapid spread of the virus than in previous outbreaks. Containment has been especially difficult because no vaccine or treatment has been developed specifically for the Bundibugyo strain, which kills about half of the people it infects. Earlier this month, the World Health Organization approved clinical trials of two new Ebola vaccines and said it expected results in early 2027. Cases have now been reported in East, Central and West Africa, giving it the widest geographic spread of any Ebola outbreak on the continent to date.

items.title: Market conditions: Dangote Cement rescinds plan to list shares on London Stock Exchange
items.description: By Peter Egwuatu Dangote Cement Plc, has rescinded plan to list its shares on the London Stock Exchange, LSE following market conditions. The company disclosed this after its Board Meeting held on Tuesday. In a statement sent to the Nigerian Exchange Limited, NGX and signed by Edward Imoedemhe Company Secretary, stated: “ This is to inform the Exchange, investing public and all stakeholders that at the meeting of the Board of Directors of Dangote Cement PLC held today, 10 November 2026, the Board resolved that, in light of current market conditions and the company’s strategic priorities, the company announces that it and its selling shareholder, Dangote Industries Limited (DIL) will not proceed with the proposed secondary listing and offering on the London Stock Exchange at this time. “ The company’s ordinary shares remain listed on the NGX, and this decision does not in any way affect the company’s operations or business plans. “Dangote Cement PLC remains focused on delivering sustainable value to its shareholders and building on its strong market position.” It will be recalled that Dangote had disclosed plans to list the cement business on the London Stock Exchange in May, eight years after an earlier attempt in 2018 failed. He had told the Financial Times that the proposed dual listing would involve selling about 10 percent of Dangote Cement’s shares on the UK exchange. items.title: Dr Nyaho-Tamakloe: Celebrating Hearts of Oak’s 115 years of history, excellence and institutional development
items.description: Today, as Accra Hearts of Oak Sporting Club celebrates its 115th anniversary, I consider it a great honour to join the entire Phobian fraternity, both in Ghana and across the world, in commemorating the remarkable journey of one of Africa’s most distinguished football institutions. This anniversary provides an important opportunity to reflect upon our history, celebrate our achievements, appreciate the sacrifices of those who have contributed to our development and renew our collective commitment to building a stronger institution for future generations. The history of Accra Hearts of Oak dates back to 11 November 1911, when a group of visionary young men in Accra, led by Christopher Brandford Nettey, popularly known as Asafoatse Nettey, established a football club that would eventually become a symbol of sporting excellence, unity and resilience. From its humble beginnings in colonial Accra, Hearts of Oak has grown into a nationally and internationally recognised institution whose influence extends far beyond football. Our famous colours of red, yellow and blue, together with our enduring motto, “Never Say Die Until the Bones Are Rotten,” have become powerful expressions of determination, courage and an unyielding spirit. Over the decades, Hearts of Oak has distinguished itself through numerous domestic and continental achievements, including the historic 2000 CAF Champions League triumph, the 2001 CAF Super Cup victory and the 2004 CAF Confederation Cup success. These accomplishments, together with our many Ghana Premier League and FA Cup titles, have firmly established our place in African football history. We remember with gratitude the generations of outstanding players, coaches, administrators and supporters whose sacrifices made these achievements possible, particularly the legendary players of the Musical Youth era and the celebrated 64 Battalion. My personal association with Hearts of Oak has been one of unwavering commitment to discipline, institutional development and the pursuit of excellence. Having served the club in various capacities, including as Chairman of the Interim Management Committee in 1986, I have witnessed its moments of glory as well as its periods of difficulty. These experiences have strengthened my conviction that the greatness of Hearts of Oak must never be measured solely by trophies, but also by the strength of its institutions, the integrity of its administration and its ability to develop successive generations of footballers. APPRECIATION TO THE BOARD, MANAGEMENT AND STAFF On this historic occasion, I wish to express my profound appreciation to our Executive Board Chairman, Togbe Afede XIV , for his vision, leadership and sustained commitment to the development of Accra Hearts of Oak. His contribution to the club’s infrastructural transformation deserves particular recognition, especially his determination to establish permanent facilities that will strengthen the club’s administrative, commercial and sporting capacities. I equally acknowledge the contributions of the current Board of Directors, past board members and all those who have provided financial, professional and strategic support to the institution. Their collective efforts have helped position Hearts of Oak for a future in which sustainable development and modern administration must become essential pillars of our operations. My sincere appreciation also goes to my colleagues on the Interim Management Committee, the administrative staff, technical teams, coaches, medical personnel, academy officials, security officers, groundskeepers and all employees who continue to work diligently for the progress of the club. Every successful institution depends upon the dedication of individuals whose contributions may not always attract public recognition, and I wish to assure them that their sacrifices are deeply appreciated. PHOBIA HOUSE AND THE KPOBIMAN ACADEMY: A LEGACY FOR FUTURE GENERATIONS One of the most significant developments in the modern history of Hearts of Oak is the investment in permanent infrastructure, particularly the redevelopment of our headquarters, popularly known as Phobia House , and the establishment of the Hearts Africa Football Academy and Sports Complex at Kpobiman . The redevelopment of Phobia House into a modern administrative and commercial facility represents an important milestone in our institutional development. The facility provides modern office accommodation and commercial spaces, with provision for preserving the club’s rich history through a museum and heritage centre. Beyond its architectural significance, the headquarters represents an investment in administrative efficiency, commercial sustainability and the long-term preservation of our institutional identity. I wish to commend Togbe Afede XIV, the Board of Directors, the project consultants, engineers, architects, financiers and contractors who contributed to this achievement. Special recognition goes to Rema Alma, the construction company responsible for delivering the new headquarters, and its leadership, including Madam Emilia Ahadzi, for their contributions towards the successful completion and handover of the facility. Equally important is the Hearts Africa Football Academy and Sports Complex at Kpobiman, which represents a major investment in youth development and the future competitiveness of our club. The complex has been designed to provide a comprehensive environment for football training, education, accommodation, physical conditioning and recreation. Its facilities and development plans encompass natural grass and artificial turf football pitches, residential accommodation for academy players, classrooms, administrative offices, a gymnasium, dining facilities, changing rooms and other essential sporting infrastructure. The inclusion of a swimming pool, golf course, tennis and basketball facilities , together with plans for a mini-stadium and hospitality infrastructure, demonstrates the broader vision of developing Kpobiman into a modern, multipurpose sporting complex. These facilities, as they are progressively completed and operationalised, will provide opportunities for athletic development, recreation, rehabilitation and sustainable commercial activities. I wish to express my appreciation to everyone who has contributed to these projects, particularly Togbe Afede XIV, the Board of Directors, project managers, architects, engineers, construction companies, artisans, technical personnel, financiers and the Kpobiman community. Their collective efforts have laid an important foundation for the future of Hearts of Oak. However, we must recognise that infrastructure alone cannot guarantee success. These investments must be supported by professional management, qualified personnel, regular maintenance, financial discipline and a clear commitment to developing talented young footballers. OUR SUPPORTERS AND THE FUTURE OF HEARTS OF OAK I cannot conclude without acknowledging the extraordinary loyalty of our supporters, whose passion and sacrifices have sustained Hearts of Oak throughout its 115-year history. From the National Chapters Committee to our supporters’ organisations across Ghana and abroad, the Phobian fraternity remains an indispensable part of our institutional identity. I encourage every supporter to continue demonstrating loyalty, discipline, unity and constructive engagement, recognising always that the interests of Hearts of Oak must remain greater than those of any individual or group. As we celebrate this anniversary, we must also remind ourselves that the achievements of the past impose upon us a responsibility to secure the future. Our ambition must be to build a professionally managed, financially sustainable and internationally competitive football institution, supported by strong youth development structures, modern infrastructure and an administrative culture founded upon integrity, accountability and excellence. I pay special tribute to our founding fathers, departed patrons, former chairmen, directors, administrators, players, coaches and supporters whose sacrifices established and preserved the institution we proudly celebrate today. Their legacy must continue to inspire our decisions and guide our actions. To Togbe Afede XIV, the Board of Directors, my colleagues on the Interim Management Committee, management, staff, players, supporters and the entire Phobian family, I extend my heartfelt congratulations and sincere gratitude for your continued commitment to our beloved club. After 115 years, the oak tree still stands. Its roots remain firmly established in the sacrifices of our founding fathers, its branches continue to extend across generations, and its enduring spirit remains an inspiration to millions. Happy 115th Anniversary to Accra Hearts of Oak Sporting Club! Long live Hearts of Oak! Long live the Phobian fraternity! NEVER SAY DIE UNTIL THE BONES ARE ROTTEN! DR. NYAHO NYAHO-TAMAKLOE Chairman, Interim Management Committee Accra Hearts of Oak Sporting Club 11 November 2026

items.title: Contrôle des produits de grande consommation: des bouteilles de gaz subventionné saisies dans des restaurants
items.description: La Brigade mobile de contrôle économique et de la répression des fraudes (BMCRF), en collaboration avec la Brigade Labaal, a mené une opération de contrôle dans plusieurs restaurants de Ouagadougou, mardi 10 novembre 2026. L’objectif est de mettre fin à l’utilisation abusive du gaz butane subventionné, exclusivement destiné aux ménages. Le gaz butane subventionné est destiné à faciliter l’accès des ménages à cette source d’énergie. Pourtant, certains professionnels de la restauration continuent de recourir à ces bouteilles, au mépris de la réglementation en vigueur. Pour mettre un terme à cette pratique, la Brigade mobile de contrôle économique et de la répression des fraudes (BMCRF), en collaboration avec la Brigade Labaal, a effectué des contrôles dans plusieurs restaurants de Ouagadougou, le mardi 10 novembre 2026. Selon le coordonnateur général de la BMCRF, Sanibè Faho, cette opération s’inscrit dans le cadre de l’intensification des contrôles des produits de grande consommation. Elle vise, a-t-il indiqué, à assainir le marché, à garantir la disponibilité des produits et à lutter contre les pratiques spéculatives. Il a déploré certaines pratiques frauduleuses, notamment le reconditionnement et l’utilisation détournée du gaz butane subventionné, qui ont contribué, par le passé, à provoquer des pénuries au détriment des ménages. Il a rappelé que les bouteilles de gaz subventionné, dont les capacités vont de 1 à 12,5 kg, sont exclusivement réservées à l’usage domestique. En revanche, les acteurs économiques et les professionnels sont tenus d’utiliser des bouteilles spécifiques, dites « hors gabarit », non subventionnées et d’une capacité de plus 15 kg. Au cours de l’opération, plusieurs bouteilles de gaz ont été saisies dans des restaurants. Sanibè Faho a précisé qu’un délai avait été accordé aux distributeurs afin qu’ils prennent les dispositions nécessaires pour rendre disponibles les bouteilles destinées aux consommateurs professionnels à la fin du mois d’octobre 2026. Le coordonnateur général de la BMCRF a prévenu que les opérations de contrôle ne se limiteront pas aux établissements de restauration. Elles concerneront bientôt les transporteurs qui, selon lui, recourent de plus en plus au gaz subventionné dans le cadre de leurs activités. « Les contrôles vont s’étendre aux transporteurs qui utilisent de plus en plus le gaz subventionné dans leurs activités », a-t-il déclaré. Face à cette situation, Sanibè Faho a invité l’ensemble des acteurs professionnels à se conformer aux réformes engagées par l’Etat en matière d’utilisation du gaz butane. Il les a ainsi exhortés à respecter les dispositions réglementaires au risque de s’exposer à des sanctions. Adama SAWADOGO Aïssatou DIARRA (Stagiaire)

items.title: Crise au Sahel : la voix des intellectuels noirs africains manque gravement
items.description: Dans la crise que traverse le Sahel, le démographe et économiste, Clément Roger Yaméogo, interroge la contribution des intellectuels noirs africains. Nous vous proposons sa réflexion en intégralité. Depuis une dizaine d’années, trois pays du Sahel (Burkina Faso, Mali et Niger) sont en proie à l’insécurité liée au terrorisme. Pour les uns, c’est un conflit entre bergers nomades et cultivateurs sédentaires sur fond ethnique qui se disputent la raréfaction des terres. Pour d’autres, c’est un conflit de légitimité démocratique autour du pouvoir d’Etat entre les partisans de la démocratie politique de type occidentale et les partisans des régimes militaires ; enfin, certains y voient une crise interne entre les jeunes officiers et les anciens dignitaires de l’armée. Rien n’est à écarter d’emblée, toutefois, en regardant un peu la géo politique, les enjeux sont plus importants : ceux autour des immenses ressources de matières premières du Sahel que les nouvelles élites politiques africaines veulent protéger contre l’exploitation des firmes occidentales. Alors, des alliances tactiques se nouent entre les Occidentaux et les groupes terroristes. Ils mènent le même combat mais avec des objectifs différents : tandis que les groupes terroristes veulent instaurer dans la région du Sahel l’islam politique ou bien revendiquer des parties de territoires comme au nord du Mali, les Européens veulent s’assurer un approvisionnement bon marché en matières premières stratégiques comme le pétrole, l’uranium, le manganèse, l’or, le lithium, le cobalt, etc. Un chef d’Etat européen a déclaré à ses ambassadeurs : « Le Mali, c’est pour nous », si bien que la bataille sera sans doute plus longue et plus intense pour plusieurs raisons. Depuis le congrès de Berlin, le 15 novembre 1885 sous l’initiative du Chancelier allemand Otto Von Bismarck, l’Afrique fut partitionnée au profit des puissances coloniales et les ressources minières sous leur contrôle. Quand bien même les pays de la sous-région voudraient attirer d’autres investisseurs, l’insécurité obère toute initiative d’investissement qui pourrait provenir de l’Est-Russie – ou de l’Asie-Chine-particulièrement. L’insécurité devient un facteur de blocage, de conservation des ressources naturelles en l’état. De plus, il faut signaler que nulle part ailleurs, les firmes européennes ne peuvent encore avoir les avantages qu’elles ont en Afrique noire. En effet, les anciennes colonies asiatiques sont développées et protégées par la Chine et le Japon : l’Amérique latine est sous le contrôle de l’Oncle Sam. Ce faisant, alimenter une insécurité guerrière autour du Liptako Gourma devient un moyen de conservation, un impératif de survie économique à moyen terme pour l’exploitation des richesses naturelles. Ce d’autant plus que les prospectives économiques de l’Europe 2040 réalisées par la CIA/NCI1 ne sont pas favorables. En effet, selon cette étude prospective, l’Europe est caractérisée par : une démographie vieillissante, un déséquilibre économique croissant, une perte de compétitivité, un retard technologique dans l’intelligence artificielle et une perte d’influence géopolitique. Perdre l’Afrique, le dernier espoir, devient alors tout perdre. Autant, c’est une guerre pour la survie à moyen terme de l’Europe, autant c’est une guerre pour la survie à long terme des jeunes nations africaines du Sahel qui émargent actuellement au bas de l’échelle des indices de développement humain durable. Ces pays africains luttent pour l’appropriation de leurs richesses naturelles données gratuitement par Dieu pour leur développement, fussent-t-il passer par la guerre. Dans cet enjeu existentiel, il est curieux de constater que ces trois pays-Burkina Mali Niger- semblent abandonnés à leur destin. Que des organisations comme la CEDEAO ou l’Union africaine ou même des pays voisins ne s’en meuvent pas, n’étonne personne. Leurs intérêts sont ailleurs. Seulement, ce qui nous semble gênant, c’est le silence des intellectuels africains noirs dans ce combat pour l’indépendance économique. Généralement en pareilles circonstances, quand le pays est attaqué, c’est l’occasion d’une union sacrée autour de l’essentiel pour sauver la patrie contre les envahisseurs ; tel a été le cas de la position des intellectuels français à la seconde Guerre mondiale, et aussi à la guerre de décolonisation de l’Algérie où les intellectuels ont joué leur partition. Pourtant, nos intellectuels silencieux en Afrique noire ont plusieurs raisons de s’engager dans cette bataille : Ils connaissent et maitrisent mieux que quiconque les enjeux comme nous l’avions souligné plus haut ; de plus, les ressources humaines existent dans toutes les disciplines, à même d’éclairer, de tenir un discours objectif, rationnel patriotique pour la mobilisation sociale ; enfin plus qu’autrefois, les outils de diffusion comme les médias de toute nature, Internet, les réseaux sociaux existent à profusion et sont accessibles pour la majorité des populations africaines. Maintenant que nous menons une guerre existentielle, pourquoi ce mutisme ou cette faible audition des intellectuels noirs africains ? Est-ce par ignorance de leur rôle dans la société en crise ? Est-ce par ignorance des enjeux économiques et géopolitiques ? Est-ce par peur d’être incompris ou de l’environnement politique ? Est-ce par compromissions ? Est-ce par simple appréciation que la guerre est l’affaire des militaires uniquement ? Quel idéal de société poursuivent les intellectuels noirs africains ? Comment peut-on atteindre cet idéal sans combat ? Autant de questions qu’on est en droit de se poser sur le mutisme ou la faible audition des intellectuels noirs africains de l’Alliance des Etats du Sahel ou même d’ailleurs. Qu’on ne se fasse pas d’illusion, cette crise ne se limite pas aux seuls pays du Sahel ; elle a vocation à s’étendre vers les pays du Sud jusqu’à l’océan atlantique, si les mêmes conditions sont remplies, à savoir une remise en cause des intérêts occidentaux et la progression du projet de l’islam politique. En interrogeant l’histoire, on se rend compte que toutes les sociétés humaines ont évolué en dents de scies, et ont connu des hauts et des bas. Malgré tout, elles ont su toujours trouver les ressorts endogènes pour rebondir. Par exemple, dans l’antiquité, les Grecs ont dominé les Arabes ; certains Grecs avaient des esclaves arabes dans leurs concessions. A la faveur du déclin du monde gréco romain au IVe siècle, les Arabes préislamiques ont profité du savoir grec et des leurs pour développer leurs villes, le commerce, l’agriculture, les sciences et l’artisanat dans un Moyen Orient florissant, multi culturel et religieux. Les Arabes après les conquêtes islamiques à partir du VIIe siècle ont connu leur apogée jusqu’au XIIe siècle. Ils sont dominés par l’Europe dans sa partie Sud (Espagne, Portugal, Italie, France). Les Européens, profitant du déclin du monde arabo musulman ont pris « leur revanche ». Ils se sont instruits de l’intelligence et du savoir-faire gréco-romains ; pillé les bibliothèques et copié l’art et les sciences développées par les Arabes, et introduit l’énergie (charbon puis pétrole) dans leur mode de production, pour leur développement. Enfin, les Juifs ont été de tout le temps, pendant 20 siècles, les damnés de la terre en Europe. En effet, accusés d’avoir tué Jésus, de pratiques usuraires, et de culture secrète, ils ont subi un antisémitisme, qui a conduit au projet de leur extermination à la seconde Guerre mondiale par l’Allemagne sous le nazisme. Les gouvernements et les populations européennes ont participé activement à ce génocide Juif faisant de milliers de victimes. De cette douloureuse épreuve, les Juifs se sont reconstruits à travers des lobbying puissants dans tous les pays et dans tous les domaines. Aujourd’hui Israël avec l’aide de la France est une puissance nucléaire. Ils ont su se relever et se faire respecter et compter dans le concert des nations. Chaque société sur la base de son passé aussi douloureux soit-il, a su rebondir, créer une conscience positive forte, des valeurs pour se reconstruire positivement. Il aurait dû en être de même pour l’Afrique, mais hélas… ! Pourquoi, en est-il autrement ? En effet, l’Afrique noire a subi toutes les humiliations de la traite des Noirs par les Arabes et les Européens pendant des siècles, puis la colonisation et la néo colonisation des Occidentaux, pendant plus de 10 siècles. Pourquoi tout ce martyr ne révolte-t-il pas les Noirs africains ? Nous pouvons avouer que par le passé, les populations n’étaient pas éduquées, leur connaissance des enjeux était limitée aussi ; malgré tout, ils se sont battus contre l’occupant colonial malgré les moyens limités. Le déficit culturel et éducationnel est comblé actuellement par la démocratisation de l’éducation où les intellectuels africains noirs ont fréquenté les mêmes universités, obtenus les mêmes diplômes que les autres races. Alors, pourquoi les mêmes faits ne produisent pas les mêmes effets en Afrique noire ? Quel levier faudra-t-il actionner pour réveiller les intellectuels africains noirs ? Dans le cas d’espèce, comment expliquer le fait que quand bien même les envahisseurs veulent retirer par la force nos terres, nos richesses données par Dieu, suscite une réaction molle ou pas du tout, des Africains noirs, surtout de ses intellectuels censés être les lumières et les guides ? Nous manque-t-il un ressort ou bien notre ressort est-il définitivement cassé ? Cette question mérite d’être posée d’autant plus que les ressources humaines, les outils, l’objet existent. En effet, depuis 1968, année de la création du CAMES, l’Afrique noire a produit des intellectuels de haut niveau par milliers dans plusieurs domaines de la connaissance scientifique ; des ordres professionnels comme les avocats, les experts comptables, les ordres religieux, les associations de magistrats, des experts nationaux (PEN) sont des centres potentiels de réflexions dont les produits peuvent alimenter positivement le débat public sur la crise. Les universités publiques et privées par milliers sont des centres de productions intellectuelles. S’il est vrai que le diplôme ne fait de quelqu’un un intellectuel qui veut impacter positivement sa société que par sa production des idées, il n’en demeure pas moins que la recherche du diplôme permet d’avoir non seulement la maitrise des concepts, mais aussi le cadre analytique. De plus, la communication est rendue facile et accessible à tous avec les moyens électroniques bon marché pour démocratiser les connaissances. Que faire, la grande question de Lénine ? Dans cette crise, les sociologues et les anthropologues pourraient nous renseigner sur qui sont les groupes qui nous attaquent, leurs origines, leurs prétentions, leurs jeux d’alliance nationale et internationale, leurs différents appuis, leurs sources de financement, leurs sources d’information, leurs complicités internes. Ils peuvent plancher sur les fractures sociales entre communautés vivant auparavant ensemble et les déterminants de ces fractures. Les géographes devraient nous tracer, leurs itinéraires, les lieux de concentration de rassemblement, les mouvements dans l’espace des terroristes. Les historiens peuvent nous éclairer sur l’histoire des rapports humains : y a-t-il eu par le passé des crises de cette nature ? Si oui, comment ont-elles été résolues ? Les philosophes et les universitaires se doivent, avec ces éléments, élaborer un discours rational intelligible, pour déconstruire les arguments des terroristes et des Occidentaux dans leur projet de recolonisation de l’Afrique noire, et susciter un engagement nationaliste au combat. Ce discours panafricaniste devrait être porté au-delà de l’AES et toucher tout le monde noir, jusqu’à la diaspora africaine. Les journalistes devraient élaborer un plan de communication pour déconstruire l’idéologie occidentale et terroriste de la guerre au Sahel. Diffuser des messages à travers les différents médias, dans toutes les langues ; organiser des conférences, des débats populaires ; créer des revues spécialisées popularisées sur la crise pourrait être d’un apport inestimable. Les ingénieurs se pencheront sur la construction de moyens militaires moins couteux à la disposition des armées combattantes, etc. Quant aux économistes, ils devraient s’orienter sur l’économie de la reconstruction, des réparations. Les archivistes devraient s’organiser pour conserver les archives, les objets historiques et culturels, les documents de la mémoire collective du pays pour les épargner de la destruction des groupes terroristes. Les religieux ne doivent pas rester en reste, car, c’est une guerre juste au sens de l’Islam et du Christianisme développée par Saint Augustin à la fin du IVe siècle, suivie de Saint Thomas d’Aquin au moyen âge : des gens attaquent les lieux de culte, tuent les fidèles et les guides religieux innocents, pillent les biens et les objets de culte ; alors le droit à la défense devient légitime et impératif. Cette guerre est militaire mais peut se gagner par la communication. Pour rien au monde, les Européens ne vont pas abandonner « leur chose ». La domination par la violence est dans la culture occidentale un héritage de la civilisation gréco romaine qui forme le socle de la pensée politique de l’Europe institutionnelle. Ils n’ont rien abandonné des conclusions du congrès de Berlin de 1885 dans le fonds. Par une espèce de myopie stratégique, l’institutionnel européen ne se rend pas compte des changements, des mutations en cours dans le monde africain noir. D’ailleurs, tant mieux pour nous Africains noirs. Si tous les Africains noirs, organisent une propagande nationale, objective, non anti européen, mais anti exploitation de leurs richesses naturelles, tout en cherchant de nouvelles alliances stratégiques, l’Europe pourrait reformuler sa perception de l’Afrique noire actuellement. L’avenir est au continent noir, jeune, ayant plusieurs alliances stratégiques au choix et pouvant bénéficier des découvertes scientifiques existantes pour son développement. Tout est là pour que l’Afrique noire accélère ses transformations sociales, et entre positivement désormais dans l’histoire. Clément Roger YAMEOGO Démographe-Economiste Cabinet CERYA https://cerya.org/blog/

items.title: PM Shehbaz to join other world leaders at COP31 today, will outline Pakistan’s climate priorities
items.description: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif is set to highlight Pakistan’s climate priorities at the COP31 Antalya Leaders’ Summit in Turkiye today, with other world leaders joining him in setting out their climate priorities. Delegates from nearly 200 countries are meeting in the Mediterranean resort city of Antalya as global greenhouse gas emissions show little sign of falling and wars, inflation and other crises compete for political attention. The world leaders will begin their speeches in the afternoon and continue through the day on Thursday, according to the COP31 schedule. Wednesday’s speakers are also expected to include Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, who was re-elected at the end of ​October, and whose country hosted last year’s climate talks. European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen, Chinese Vice President Han Zheng, and Marshall Islands ​President Hilda Heine will also speak on Wednesday. The United States, the world’s largest historical emitter, has skipped the talks for the second year in a ‌row after ⁠President Donald Trump — who has called global warming a hoax — withdrew the US from climate cooperation following his return to office in 2025. For his part, PM Shehbaz will highlight Pakistan’s climate priorities and emphasise the urgent need for enhanced global climate action and strengthened international cooperation to mitigate the adverse impacts of climate change, the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO) said following the premier’s arrival in Turkiye on Tuesday night. The Foreign Office (FO) has said the prime minister will also highlight “Pakistan’s steps towards rapid solarisation and expansion of its renewable energy capacity, as part of its transition towards a cleaner and more resilient economy, along with its efforts to strengthen disaster preparedness and early-warning systems”. He will call for predictable, adequate and accessible climate finance for developing countries to strengthen their resilience and pursue sustainable development, it added. PM Shehbaz will also address a high-level dialogue on clean energy transition and electrification convened by the COP31 presidency, titled “ 35 by 35: Powering the Future ” and scheduled for 3pm local time (5pm Pakistan time). On the sidelines of the summit, the prime minister is scheduled to hold bilateral meetings with Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan and other world leaders attending COP31 to discuss matters of mutual interest and explore avenues for strengthening bilateral cooperation. According to PMO, a “Pakistan Pavilion” has been established at the COP31 venue where 54 events will be hosted on various themes. ‘Difficult start’ Ahead of the conference, negotiators had been locked in discussions late on Sunday over demands by developing nations to include items on climate finance in the official agenda. “This has already been a difficult start for COP31,” said Jasper Inventor, head of Greenpeace’s COP31 delegation. Under UN climate agreements, developed countries, which are historically responsible for most greenhouse gas emissions, have provided financial support to help developing nations adapt to climate impacts and transition to cleaner energy. But poorer countries say the sums remain insufficient. Inventor said developed countries were “taking a hard line” over whether to include a platform, agreed at COP30 in Brazil last year , aimed at discussing how wealthy nations should provide funds to developing nations. African countries are also pushing for the agenda to include discussions on the tripling of adaptation finance, which aims to help poorer nations pay for measures such as building sea walls or planting drought-resistant crops. Observers say few major breakthroughs are expected at COP31 as countries grapple with an oil price shock and geopolitical tensions fuelled by the US war on Iran and Russia’s conflict in Ukraine. As negotiators tussled in Antalya, the UN’s World Meteorological Organisation released a report indicating that 2026 has continued a streak of exceptional global temperatures, melting ice and rising sea levels. The EU’s climate monitor warned last week that 2026 would most likely be the second-hottest year ever recorded , while scientists say 2027 could top the chart, fuelled by El Nino.

items.title: Fight or flight? Trump mixes signals after midterms
items.description: President Donald Trump’s political mantra is “fight, fight, fight.” But he has given decidedly mixed messages about whether he will do so after Republicans were hammered in the midterms. In the week since becoming a lame duck , Trump named the hardline architect of his migration crackdown as his chief of staff, while admitting his deportation policy was too tough. The 80-year-old raised eyebrows when he publicly asked Ultimate Fighting Championship boss Dana White to be his new press secretary — then claimed he was just joking. He has admitted that the Iran war was largely to blame for the midterms rout. But he has strongly backed Pentagon chief Pete Hegseth’s battle against impeachment. And despite saying on election night that he’d accept the results of the Democratic sweep, he has reverted to type and revived baseless claims of election fraud. “One of the characteristics of Donald Trump is that he changes his mind on a dime,” Democratic Senator Chris Coons told CNN. “He’ll be praising someone on Monday, firing them on Tuesday, and pretending he never knew them on Wednesday. So it’s hard to predict exactly what Donald Trump is going to do.” ‘Too tough’ Democrats have promised to rein in Trump and launch a series of investigations into corruption and abuse of power. He could face a third impeachment. But for a president supposedly facing his last stand, he has at times struck a surprisingly conciliatory tone. As results came in, he congratulated Democrats on seizing Congress and said he could work with them. Instead of a press conference the next day, he gave reporters a tour of his new White House ballroom — sparking speculation he might spend the rest of his term on his building projects. But the signs of volatility were still there. In the Oval Office, Trump placed a red baseball cap saying “veto” on his desk. And when Trump announced on Friday that ultraloyalist Stephen Miller would replace Susie Wiles as his chief of staff, it seemed that the gloves were finally off. The brains behind the masked immigration raids that left two Americans dead, Miller has also been instrumental in using executive orders to help Trump bypass Congress. Yet in an interview the same day — though broadcast on Sunday — Trump conceded voters had been turned off by the aggressive deportation push. “I think it was too tough,” Trump told the CBS News “60 Minutes” program. Still, the chances of Trump doing a deal with Democrats — possibly even for an amnesty for undocumented migrants — remain low. “It doesn’t seem likely. Not with this decision to have Stephen Miller running the show,” Sarah Binder, a senior fellow in governance studies at the Brookings Institution, said in a panel discussion this week. ‘Violent fighter’ Trump’s astonishing announcement on Saturday that he wanted “violent fighter and warrior” Dana White to be his new spokesman also seemed to signal a war footing. If it seemed too ironic to be true, it was. A day later Trump said he was “kidding.” Ever the showman, the former reality TV star brought the UFC boss to the White House podium for an unexpected visit on Monday, where White turned down the job. The administration’s biggest fight now is against Hegseth’s impeachment. It’s a fight Trump appears to be joining with relish — saying that Hegseth “gets an ‘A’ PLUS, PLUS, PLUS” shortly after the Pentagon chief gave a press conference calling the charges a “farce.” But Hegseth will know that Trump is rarely shy of shaking up his staff. He jettisoned Wiles just over two weeks after saying there was “zero chance” he would sack her. And Trump himself admitted he isn’t likely to change his stripes. Asked by CBS if he could forgive his foes, when faced with going to heaven or not, he demurred. “Can I be honest? I probably cannot do that, no. Because I do hate some of my enemies, and I always will”.

items.title: Un défi sous régional
items.description: L’expulsion des orpailleurs étrangers en Guinée remet au goût du jour une problématique de l’orpaillage clandestin et de ses conséquences socioéconomiques, sécuritaires et environnementales en Afrique de l’Ouest. Si chaque Etat est souverain dans la gestion de ses ressources naturelles et dans la réglementation des activités exercées sur son territoire, la mobilité des populations à la recherche de meilleures opportunités économiques impose néanmoins une approche concertée entre les pays de la sous-région. En effet, l’orpaillage constitue une activité économique transfrontalière qui attire chaque année des milliers de personnes en quête de revenus et de meilleures conditions de vie. Selon le point du Centre de coordination et de gestion des crises du Mali (CECOGEC), à la date du 7 novembre 2026, près de 160 000 orpailleurs refoulés de Guinée ont été accueillis à Bamako et Kouremalé. Du Burkina Faso à la Guinée, en passant par le Mali, le Niger et la Côte d’Ivoire, les mouvements de travailleurs vers les sites aurifères témoignent de l’ampleur de ce phénomène. Les frontières ne constituent donc pas un obstacle à cette mobilité qui s’organise souvent au gré des opportunités offertes par les zones d’exploitation artisanale de l’or. Toutefois, lorsque cette activité s’exerce en dehors des cadres légaux, elle peut engendrer de nombreuses difficultés pour les pays d’accueil. Occupation anarchique des sites, dégradation de l’environnement, pollution des cours d’eau, insécurité, conflits fonciers et exploitation des personnes vulnérables sont autant de conséquences auxquelles les autorités doivent faire face. Dès lors, la décision d’un Etat de réorganiser son secteur minier artisanal, de lutter contre l’exploitation illégale de ses ressources ou de faire respecter sa réglementation relève de ses prérogatives souveraines. Cependant, la gestion de ces situations ne saurait se limiter à des mesures d’expulsion. Derrière les chiffres et les opérations de déguerpissement, se trouvent des hommes et des femmes, parfois accompagnés de leurs familles, dont les moyens de subsistance dépendent de cette activité. Une expulsion, lorsqu’elle n’est pas accompagnée de dispositions appropriées, peut exposer ces populations à la précarité, aux difficultés de transport et à d’autres formes de vulnérabilité. C’est pourquoi, la protection de la dignité humaine doit demeurer une préoccupation essentielle dans la conduite de telles opérations. Au-delà du cas guinéen, cette situation interpelle ainsi l’ensemble des Etats de la sous-région. Il serait illusoire de penser que chaque pays pourra résoudre, à lui seul, un phénomène alimenté par la mobilité transfrontalière des populations et les disparités économiques entre les territoires. Les gouvernements gagneraient à renforcer leur coopération à travers des mécanismes de concertation, d’échanges d’informations et de coordination des politiques minières et migratoires. Une telle démarche permettrait de mieux encadrer la mobilité des travailleurs, de lutter efficacement contre les réseaux d’exploitation clandestine et de prévenir les déplacements désorganisés de populations. Elle devrait également favoriser la sensibilisation des candidats à l’orpaillage sur les exigences légales des pays d’accueil et les risques liés à l’exploitation artisanale non réglementée. En outre, les Etats pourraient réfléchir à des mécanismes communs de protection et d’assistance aux ressortissants confrontés à des situations de détresse à l’étranger. Dans cette dynamique, la solidarité manifestée par les Burkinabè autour du rapatriement de leurs compatriotes constitue un motif de satisfaction. La mobilisation des autorités, des structures concernées et des bonnes volontés pour accompagner ces personnes traduit un sens de responsabilité et de fraternité nationale. Elle rappelle que la protection des citoyens ne s’arrête pas aux frontières du territoire national. Lorsqu’un compatriote se retrouve en difficulté à l’étranger, la solidarité collective doit pouvoir s’exprimer, au-delà des considérations individuelles. Cette mobilisation mérite d’autant plus d’être encouragée qu’elle contribue à préserver la dignité des personnes concernées et à faciliter leur retour dans leur pays. Elle témoigne également de la nécessité pour les communautés nationales de rester attentives au sort de leurs ressortissants vivant ou travaillant à l’étranger. Le Burkina Faso, en accompagnant ses ressortissants, donne un exemple de responsabilité nationale. Mais pour que de telles situations ne deviennent pas récurrentes, les Etats de la sous-région doivent aller au-delà des réactions ponctuelles et construire une véritable stratégie commune. Car, la solidarité entre les peuples et la coopération entre les Etats demeurent les meilleures voies pour concilier souveraineté, sécurité et dignité humaine. Soumaïla BONKOUNGOU

items.title: Nigéria : l’opposition en difficulté
items.description: Au Nigéria, les Etats-majors des partis politiques s’activent pour la présidentielle de janvier 2027, qui verra la succession ou la réélection du chef de l’Etat, Bola Tinubu, en quête d’un second mandat, face à 17 autres candidats. Alors qu’il faisait partie de la liste officielle des prétendants publiée par la Commission électorale, l’ancien vice-président, Atiku Aboubakar, 80 ans, qui avait déjà lancé sa campagne, a vu sa candidature invalidée récemment par la Haute Cour de justice d’Abuja. C ette juridiction a estimé, que les décisions prises au nom de son parti, le Congrès démocratique africain (ADC), par l’actuel Président, David Mark, sont de nul effet, y compris celle concernant sa désignation comme candidat à la future présidentielle. En lice pour la 7e fois au scrutin présidentiel, l’ancien dirigeant des Douanes de Lagos fait les frais des procédures judiciaires liées aux querelles internes de l’ADC. Atiku Abubakar, arrivé en seconde position à la présidentielle de 2023 avec 29% des voix, voit son rêve de prendre sa revanche sur Tinubu se briser. L’adversaire le plus sérieux du chef de l’Etat sortant espérait pourtant prendre le dessus l’année prochaine, mais le sort en a décidé autrement. Son poursuivant immédiat à la dernière présidentielle, Peter Obi, lui aussi ne semble pas serein dans la course, puisqu’il dénonce des actes de sabotage de sa campagne. Si la situation d’Atiku Abubakar et de Peter Obi retient l’attention, celle de l’opposition nigériane dans son ensemble inquiète. Les opposants sont convaincus, que le Président Tibunu travaille à écarter ses adversaires les plus coriaces, pour assurer sa réélection. Mais l’opposition ne peut en vouloir qu’à elle-même, dans la mesure où malgré les discours de bonne intention, elle n’ira pas en rangs serrés à la bataille pour la présidentielle. Si elle avait travaillé à une candidature commune, le camp du pouvoir allait faire face à une organisation solide, avec moins de failles à exploiter. On a d’ailleurs assisté à une vague massive de défections de l’opposition vers le parti au pouvoir, le Congrès des progressistes (APC). C’est la preuve flagrante d’un manque de cohésion dans les rangs de l’opposition, qui a contribué à renforcer la majorité présidentielle. Avec le visage moins reluisant qu’elle présente, il sera difficile pour l’opposition nigériane d’empêcher une réélection du Président Tinubu. A moins que les Nigérians, qui ont rejeté en bonne partie ses réformes économiques et critiqué sa gestion de la crise sécuritaire dans le Nord-Est, ne décident d’un vote-sanction. C’est un scenario qui n’est pas à écarter, dans la mesure où la personnalité de Tinubu est clivante. Souvent présenté comme un dirigeant au service des riches, au détriment du bas peuple, le chef de l’Etat nigérian n’a pas bonne presse chez nombre de ses compatriotes. Les récriminations sur sa gouvernance et l’étiquette de l’homme des milieux aisés peut-il compromettre son ambition de garder la main sur le pays ? Il détient une chance de rempiler, mais seuls, les électeurs décideront de ce qu’il en est en janvier 2027. Kader Patrick KARANTAO

items.title: Gbentri-Nakpanduri Road: Agbodza vows to address abandoned 40km stretch
items.description: The government is seeking a lasting solution to a 40-kilometre section of the Gbentri-Nakpanduri Road in the North East Region that was left out of the existing construction contract, creating a major break in the road project. The Minister of Roads and Highways, Kwame Governs Agbodza, expressed concern about the outstanding stretch, which he said had been left unattended following decisions taken under the previous administration. He said the omission had created a gap along the Eastern Corridor road network, with implications for motorists and other road users who depend on the route. Speaking during an inspection of the ongoing works, Mr Agbodza attributed the situation to the previous government’s handling of projects undertaken through supplier-credit arrangements. He said some contractors working under those arrangements had been allowed to reduce the scope of their contracts, leaving important sections of road projects unfinished. The minister said the resulting gaps had complicated efforts to deliver continuous road infrastructure and needed to be addressed to ensure that commuters could enjoy the full benefits of the ongoing works. He, however, assured residents and road users that the government would work towards finding a lasting solution to the 40-kilometre stretch. He said efforts would be made to address the outstanding section and ease the difficulties faced by commuters using the route. The Gbentri-Nakpanduri Road forms part of the Eastern Corridor network, an important transport link in the eastern part of the country.
