items.title: Spurring Ebonyi’s shy momentum, by Ochereome Nnanna
items.description: Ebonyi State is on my mind today for a reason. On 1st October 2026, it celebrated its 30th anniversary under the helmsmanship of Governor Francis Ogbonna Nwifuru. The late Head of State, General Sani Abacha, created six new states from each of the newly designated geopolitical zones: Ebonyi, Ekiti, Bayelsa, Nasarawa, Gombe and Zamfara. Interestingly, Nwifuru, who now sits pretty at the helm of its affairs, was only 18! Obviously, when this state was created, Nwifuru and young Ebonyians like him were tailor-made to inherit its future. The state, which was carved out of Abia and Enugu States, is the smallest by population and landmass, as well as well behind the developmental level of its four senior sisters: Abia, Imo, Enugu and Anambra. However, Ebonyi has been unusually blessed with a string of good-performing governors since 1999. On this score, only Enugu State compares. In 1999, Dr Sam Egwu, a crop scientist and celebrated academic, emerged as the first elected governor. Egwu plunged headlong into education and agriculture, establishing the Ebonyi State University. After his eight years, he handed over to a veteran administrator, Chief Martin Elechi. Elechi’s main legacies were the construction of roads and 39 “Bridges of Unity” across the state. Elechi also handed over to his former Deputy Governor, Dave Umahi, a megalomaniac who also went on to display his craft as a construction engineer, building massive institutions, including city roads, flyovers, markets, an airport (though poorly done), and the Federal University Teaching Hospital, which he painted in riotous colours and named after himself. Umahi’s airport was later abandoned, and Nwifuru had to reconstruct the runway. The revolving chair eventually settled on Rt. Hon. Francis Ogbonna Nwifuru, who served as the two-term Speaker of the Ebonyi State House of Assembly. No other Ebonyi Speaker was able to serve beyond one term. Nwifuru’s story is a classic “grass to grace” tale. He was once a mason (bricklayer). But he attended the Ebonyi State University and specialised in the building sciences. He is determined to prove his trade through concrete examples (forgive the pun). While his predecessors concentrated on the big roads and bridges, Nwifuru has chosen to fix his efforts on the interconnecting rural roads which take the people home right to their communities. He launched his 115 “two-kilometres-each” roads, complete with bridges and culverts. Many of them have been completed, while the rest are assignments for his envisaged second term in office. The logic behind this strategy is impeccable. Ebonyi State, small as it is by landmass, is one of the frontline agrarian states in the country, with its native population renowned for their deep agricultural traditions. These two-kilometre roads, when completed, will link between 230 and 300 rural communities and enable them to evacuate their agricultural products to commercial centres. This will create employment and wealth and bring millions of Ebonyi youths hawking trash in urban streets throughout Nigeria back to the land where the real wealth hides in plain sight. The government is investing heavily in tractors, the training of youth and women, the construction of markets, fertiliser production, distribution and policing against racketeering and fakery. Abandoned water projects are being revived, with new ones being constructed, particularly in Abakaliki, Ezillo, Afikpo and others. The Nwifuru administration has also paid great attention to the sector that makes the child of nobody become somebody without the special graces of somebody – education. He, like most of us, is a good example of the wonder that education can perform in a person’s life. From bricklayer to Parliamentary Speaker and Governor – can you beat that! From the recruitment of 2,000 basic education teachers to the construction of 12 classrooms each in 39 basic education schools; from the sponsorship of 1,400 Ebonyi indigenes for Master’s and PhD scholarships in UK institutions to massive investments in ICT and smart schools, Nwifuru is paving the way to lift more youths from nobody to somebody. Every sector is receiving attention. There are some areas that Governor Nwifuru and other Ebonyi ruling elite need to pay more attention to in order to hasten the human development indices. Right now, Ebonyi ranks with Sharia Muslim states in the North, such as Sokoto, Zamfara, Kebbi, Jigawa, Katsina and others, in human development indices. These are the states where governments spend huge proportions of federal allocations on the political elite, emirs and clerics. The Nwifuru government’s construction of duplexes for all traditional rulers in the state is what typical far-North states do because governance over there is “rulers first”. In Igboland, communities, not governments, build “befitting” palaces for their traditional rulers. Also, the state bears huge pension burdens of past governors. Former Governor Umahi failed to pay pensions in all of his eight years in power. He abandoned it for Nwifuru, who has now cleared it. But he enjoys his own sumptuous pension benefits. The primary focus of leadership should be to lift the poor and create an enabling environment for growing wealth from the bottom up. Nwifuru’s pro-masses agenda will achieve a lot in this direction if faithfully implemented. Ebonyi ranks more than many Igbo states in quality of governance since 1999, yet the leadership and hardworking people of the state continue to carry the image of the “shy horse” of Igboland. We must join hands to fight this misperception because no Igbo is more than the others. The leaders should take the lead by making Ebonyi State a theatre of sound education, a huge agricultural market destination and a hub of prosperity. Make Ebonyi a greener pasture. It will attract not just the indigenes whiling away their lives elsewhere in poverty; it will also magnet non-indigenes whose huge presence will be a confirmation of success. The South East is the most developed zone in human and infrastructure indices. Ebonyi must be a strong part of this story. The post Spurring Ebonyi’s shy momentum, by Ochereome Nnanna appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Anthropic launches powerful new models ahead of Wall Street debut
items.description: Anthropic announced on Monday that it would release updated versions of two of its most powerful artificial intelligence (AI) models as the company prepares for a highly anticipated IPO this month. The new models, Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2, can perform up to 30% faster than previous versions, particularly on complex tasks such as coding, while costing 20% less, the company said. Both are built on the same underlying model. Fable 5.2 has safeguards that block most cybersecurity and biology tasks, which lets Anthropic offer it to all users. Mythos 5.2 has fewer of those restrictions and is available only to vetted organizations working in cybersecurity or biomedical research. The first versions of Fable and Mythos were released under a cloud of controversy. Both models were pulled days after their June launch, when the US Commerce Department, citing national security concerns, ordered Anthropic to bar access by foreign nationals. The controls were lifted weeks later. The latest versions come as Anthropic is aiming to hold its initial public offering the week of November 16, when it is expected to raise up to $100 billion, which would make it the largest IPO on record. The San Francisco-based lab's Wall Street debut is expected to fetch a valuation exceeding $1 trillion, though estimates have fallen in recent weeks from a high of $2 trillion. The stock market debut is being seen as a gauge of how long the AI spending boom lifting the US economy can last. Growth has been staggering at the company. Anthropic's revenue reached $17 billion in the third quarter, up from just $1.4 billion a year earlier, a securities filing showed earlier this month. Sales growth slowed from previous quarters, however, amid fierce competition from ChatGPT-maker OpenAI and cheaper models, many of them from China. Anthropic also posted an operating loss of $567 million in the third quarter as it paid more for short-term computing capacity. The company’s valuation has also been weighed down by a broader market pullback after a string of quarterly earnings reports spooked investors. These raised concerned about the hundreds of billions of dollars that US tech giants are spending on AI. Democrats also regained control of Congress in the US midterms, raising investor concerns about a potential regulatory crackdown on the tech industry, including against data center buildouts. Ballot measures restricting data center construction could hamper the growth plans of AI developers such as Anthropic, as well as rivals including OpenAI, Meta, Microsoft and Google.

items.title: Arrests made in Mohamed Al Fayed probe in France, police say
items.description: French police have made arrests after three properties, including the Ritz hotel in Paris, were searched in relation to an investigation into Mohamed Al Fayed’s abuse. The Paris prosecutor’s office told the BBC that several individuals were taken into custody for questioning last month and later released. In a confidential letter sent to survivors, the Metropolitan Police said its officers were present during the searches on 13 and 14 October, in what is understood to be a joint operation between British and French authorities. It is the first time any arrests have been made in relation to alleged abuse and trafficking by the former Harrods and Ritz owner. Several victims of Al Fayed were also interviewed by French investigators, the prosecutor’s office said. It added that the searches were part of a preliminary investigation into “allegations of human trafficking committed by an organized group, aggravated pimping committed by an organized group, and rape”. The investigation is ongoing and digital material seized during the searches is being analysed. The late Egyptian billionaire bought the Ritz Paris hotel in 1979, and it is still owned by the Al Fayed family. The Villa Windsor in western Paris, another property involved in the search, was a holiday home for the Al Fayed family. It was previously the home of King Edward VIII, following his abdication, and his wife Wallis Simpson. The Met shared this statement from French authorities with victims: “At this stage of the proceedings, several victims have been interviewed by French investigators, and the investigations are being conducted in liaison with the British authorities. “In this context, searches and evidence-gathering operations were carried out in mid-October 2026, notably within the Hotel Ritz in the 1st arrondissement of Paris, as well as at the Villa Sainte-Thérèse in Saint-Tropez, a former property of Mohamed Al Fayed, and at the Villa Windsor in the 16th arrondissement of Paris, in the presence of British investigators. “Several suspects were taken into police custody, measures which were lifted following their interviews, specifically for the purpose of analyzing digital material seized during the search operations. “The investigations are continuing under the direction of the Paris Public Prosecutor’s Office.” A Met Police spokesperson confirmed its officers travelled to France in October and were present during the operation. The Ritz hotel in Paris is still owned by the Al Fayed family Al Fayed, who died in 2023 aged 94, was accused by more than 20 women of sexual assault in a BBC documentary and podcast in September 2024. One of the women featured in the documentary said she was sexually assaulted by Al Fayed at the Ritz hotel in Paris, while another woman said she had been raped by him at the Villa Windsor residence. Since those allegations, more than 400 alleged victims or witnesses have come forward to lawyers. A woman has also told BBC Scotland she was trafficked, drugged, sexually assaulted and held prisoner on the Balnagown Estate by Al Fayed’s brother , Salah Fayed, who died in 2010. Both brothers died without facing legal charges in relation to these allegations. Earlier this year, Police Scotland said it was carrying out further investigations into allegations connected to Balnagown Estate. In a statement, a force spokesperson said: “Three people have been identified in connection with offending against a number of victims. “Our inquiries are ongoing and it would be inappropriate to comment further.” The Justice for Fayed and Harrods Survivors group said it welcomed the “significant developments” and cooperation between the Met and French authorities. “We believe that all properties owned by Fayed should be investigated with the same thoroughness as those already searched, wherever they are located, to ensure that no potentially relevant evidence is overlooked,” the group said. “We hope these developments represent meaningful progress towards identifying and holding to account all those who facilitated, concealed or assisted his offending, wherever they operated.” The survivor advocacy group No One Above said: “France is treating this as organised human trafficking, led by specialists, with properties searched and evidence seized. That is what a serious investigation into a network looks like. “Two years on, survivors are still waiting for the same from the Met. It is time the National Crime Agency took this investigation over.” The management of the Ritz Paris told AFP news agency that it “does not tolerate any form of harassment, abuse or inappropriate behaviour” and that it was ready “to cooperate fully with the competent judicial authorities”.

items.title: UN steps up Gaza aid efforts as heavy rains affect over 200,000 people
items.description: UN humanitarians said on Tuesday that they and partners are scrambling to aid more than 200,000 residents of Gaza who, according to estimates, may have been affected following the heavy rains over the weekend. Site management partners and others reported damage as of Monday to more than 40,000 family shelters and over 900 latrines. Nine health facilities also suffered damage, the UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) said. "Humanitarian partners say there are not enough places to which people in flooded areas and war-damaged buildings can relocate," OCHA said. "This is because Israeli authorities are still restricting Palestinian access anywhere behind the so-called 'Yellow Line,' which means that most of Gaza's land remains off limit." The office said its partners warn that their ability to provide timely support is limited, leaving many in poor living conditions. By Monday, support had reached about 750 households, or roughly 4,500 people. Assistance included tents, tarpaulins, blankets, plastic sheets, mattresses, cereal packages, jerrycans and hygiene kits. Israel on Tuesday blamed Hamas for the suffering of Palestinians in Gaza, saying reconstruction could not begin until the group disarmed. The remarks came a day after US President Donald Trump's Board of Peace criticized Israel for delays in allowing humanitarian supplies into the war-devastated enclave. "Hamas alone is responsible for the suffering of the people of Gaza," the statement said, adding that the group's refusal to disarm remained the main obstacle to reconstruction. Amid the crisis caused by heavy rains, Israeli attacks have continued across the Gaza Strip. Three Palestinians, including a child, were killed on Tuesday in Israeli airstrikes and gunfire, Xinhua reported, citing Palestinian security and medical sources. An Israeli drone fired at least one missile at a shelter in the Zeitoun neighborhood, southeast of Gaza City. Medical sources at al-Ahli Baptist Hospital said the strike killed two people, including a child, and wounded three others. (With input from Xinhua)

items.title: US federal authorities could have prevented Epstein crimes, report finds
items.description: Crimes committed by the late disgraced financier Jeffrey Epstein after 2005 could have been prevented were it not for “failures” by federal investigators and prosecutors, a congressional investigation has concluded. The Republican-led US House Oversight Committee on Tuesday released its final report into what it described as the “decades-long” mishandling of the criminal investigations into Epstein and his long-term associate Ghislaine Maxwell. The report’s findings are based on interviews and depositions with witnesses, government files, and financial records over a 15-month period. Epstein died in 2019 as he awaited trial on sex trafficking charges. “While some of these failures involved an exercise in poor judgment by the USAO, others appeared to be the result of Epstein’s pervasive and wide-reaching influence,” the report reads, referring to the US Attorney’s Office. It states that, rather than fully investigating allegations in other states, the USAO for the Southern District of Florida entered into an agreement with Epstein in 2007 that allowed him to evade federal prosecution. Regarding Epstein’s death in a New York prison , investigators concluded this was a result of “a series of institutional failures at the facility,” which included staffing shortages, overworked employees, poor recordkeeping, and lax security practices. Testimony the panel solicited was “unable to definitively dispel certain theories” surrounding Epstein’s death, the report states, including accounting for a lapse in surveillance footage. It found the Justice Department (DoJ) failed to communicate about document releases and that deficient redactions exposed survivors’ sensitive personal information. The DoJ has released millions of pages of Epstein-related files in response to legislation from Congress. Earlier this year, the department had to remove thousands of documents related to Epstein from its website after victims said their identities had been compromised. The report also alleges that financial institutions like American Express enabled human trafficking and immigration fraud by allowing Epstein to use decoy flights and dummy itineraries to transport foreign workers across borders. The BBC has contacted American Express for comment. The investigative panel recommended that Congress should pass legislation to prevent the weaponisation of non-disclosure agreements, which they said Epstein used to silence survivors. “Epstein operated with impunity, shielded and enabled by powerful connections and a justice system that repeatedly failed his victims,” said James Comer, the Republican chairman of the committee. He called upon the DoJ to “interview or re-interview key witnesses, investigate Epstein associates accused of criminal activity, and ensure survivors have access to their records. The department remains under bipartisan scrutiny regarding the Epstein files. In the state of New Mexico, where Epstein had a ranch, the top state prosecutor accused the DoJ of stonewalling their criminal investigation. “With all due respect, the Chairman’s recommendations have already been addressed,” a department spokesperson said in response to Comer’s report. “The Attorney General has repeatedly said that the Epstein case is not closed and there is no statute of limitations on human trafficking.” The report accuses Democrats of being “obsessed” with trying to implicate US President Donald Trump and that an “unfounded witch hunt continued without regard for the interests of survivors”. Trump has previously said he was friendly with Epstein before they fell out in 2004. The president’s name appears thousands of times in the Epstein files, but appearing in the documents does not suggest any wrongdoing. The committee’s review did not identify any documents that would implicate Trump, the report concluded. In a statement, Rep. Robert Garcia, the top Democrat on the Oversight Committee, alleged his Republican colleagues “released a report based on an incomplete investigation and zero public hearings on Jeffrey Epstein”. Garcia accused the Justice Department of withholding “over 2.5 million pages of documents”. “We will not allow the President and his allies to dismiss this investigation,” said Garcia, who is expected to lead the committee when Democrats take control of Congress in January following the recent midterm elections. The family members of one of Epstein’s most prominent accusers, the late Virginia Roberts Giuffre, thanked Comer for releasing Tuesday’s report. “A sentence from the report stands out to us: ‘Questions remain as to whether the DOJ has released all its relevant documents.’ We could not agree more and urge that all 7 million-plus files be released,” Sky and Amanda Roberts said in a statement. “There are many more individuals who have yet to be identified and brought to justice,” they said.

items.title: Three Iran-backed suspects plotted attacks including RAF Fairford incident, US says
items.description: The US Department of Justice (DOJ) has announced charges against three Iran-backed operatives that it alleges were involved in a string of plots in the US and Europe. The DOJ said Iranian agents most recently “orchestrated a terrorist plot at an air force base in the United Kingdom”, saying they were involved in the major incident in September near RAF Fairford in the UK, where US armed forces were stationed. One man, a dual Iranian-Iraqi national, is accused of communicating with contacts in the UK from a prison in New York where he is awaiting trial on previous charges. The other two are accused of doing the same from Iran. Iran has strongly denied any involvement in the RAF Fairford incident, which came to light when suspicious vans were reported near the base. Seven men have been arrested in the UK over the incident. Iranian Mohsen Mohajeri, Iraqi national Mohammad Ali al-Hassani and dual Iranian-Iraqi citizen Mohammad Baqer Saad Dawood al-Saadi were charged in an indictment unsealed on Tuesday, the DOJ said. It accuses the trio of planning attacks in Europe that were carried out under the name of a purportedly new group with the pseudonym Harakat Ashab al-Yamin al-Islamiya (The Islamic Movement of the People of the Right Hand – HAYI). “Of the 18 terrorist attacks in the spring of 2026 for which HAYI claimed responsibility in Europe, seven took place in the UK,” the DOJ statement said. It added that the attacks involved “arsons, explosives, and in one instance, a near-fatal stabbing in London of two Jewish men, including a dual US-British citizen”. Two Jewish men were stabbed in Golders Green, north London, in April. A suspect is due to stand trial next year. “This eight-count indictment shows the determination of Iran to commit terrorist attacks in Europe and the US,” FBI Director Kash Patel said. He added that one of the three “allegedly sent coded messages to assist in future acts of violence” from detention. Patel said the accused were involved in nearly 20 attempted attacks in support of Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) and the Iran-backed Iraqi militia Kataib Hezbollah. Armed police officers were posted outside the RAF Fairford base following the incident in September A major incident was declared on 27 September near the UK’s RAF Fairford base, in the Cotswolds in Gloucestershire, after three suspicious vans were seen near the airbase. No explosive materials were found in the vans, but a quantity of petrol was seized. The DOJ said that in August, al-Hassani “allegedly directed and paid associates” in the UK to “conduct preparatory steps and arrange logistics for the RAF Fairford terrorist plot”. On 22 August, al-Hassani paid one individual to “perform pre-operational surveillance of RAF Fairford’s perimeter”, the department said. In September, al-Hassani paid several people to help him prepare for the plot, the DOJ also alleged. According to its statement, this included “procuring vans and barrels of fuel, researching the purchase of chemical accelerants, including large quantities of potassium chloride, and purchasing metallic objects that could be used as explosive shrapnel”. The suspects then gave the vans an appearance of being used by a fuel delivery business and a swimming pool supply business, the DOJ stated. “On 26 September, al-Hassani allegedly tasked individuals to drive three vans, some of which were later determined to contain barrels of fuel, to the RAF Fairford base.” The DOJ also said al-Hassani was “in frequent communication” with the van drivers and helped to direct them where to drive. “At least two of the three vans, while en route to the perimeter of RAF Fairford, encountered a security roadblock and were not allowed to proceed on their intended route,” it added. It was in the very early hours of 27 September, that the vans were spotted by a local farmer who was heading home from a party, and called the police. The Iranian embassy in London has said it “categorically rejects and strongly condemns” what it called “unfounded and malicious speculations” linking Iran to the incident. Two British nationals appeared in court last month in connection with the alleged Iran-linked plot. The US withdrew all its bombers from RAF Fairford after the incident, with President Donald Trump citing “some threats” to the base as the reason. RAF Fairford has been used by the US Air Force (USAF) for decades. In recent months, the US has flown B-1 and B-52 bombers from there to the Middle East for “defensive” strikes on Iran. In July, Iran said “any base used for aggression against Iranian territory constitutes a legitimate target for our forces”.

items.description: For years, the pro-Israel lobbying group AIPAC was a US political juggernaut, but deepening voter disillusion over US-Israeli ties and wins by openly Israel-skeptic candidates in last week's midterm elections have left it reeling. items.title: Eight indicted in foreign women’s rape case
items.description: LAHORE: A sessions court on Tuesday indicted eight suspects, including one reportedly linked to a senior minister, in a case of alleged gang rape of two foreign women. All the suspects, presently in judicial custody, were produced before the trial court for the indictment proceedings. Additional District & Sessions Judge (AD&SJ) Rafaqat Ali Gondal framed the charges against the suspects, who pleaded not guilty. The judge directed the prosecution to present its witnesses on Dec 9 so the formal trial proceedings could be commenced. Separately, the judge gave the last opportunity to the prosecution to present its arguments on the post-arrest bail petitions of three of the suspects in the case. The judge observed that the prosecution had availed multiple opportunities to argue the bail petitions on one pretext or the other. The judge adjourned the bail hearing till Nov 11 (today) with a clear warning to the prosecution to present its arguments, otherwise, the petitions would be decided in light of the case record. Advocate Salman Shahid had already concluded his arguments on behalf of the petitioners/suspects. Defence-C police in its challan (investigation report) had cleared five suspects, including the one linked to the senior political figure, of sexual assault charges and implicated them in minor offences of illegal detention and extortion. The police charged three other suspects, who were allegedly low-paid employees of one of the key suspects, with sexually assaulting the women. Published in Dawn, November 11th, 2026

items.title: Development spending stalls despite surplus
items.description: ISLAMABAD: The country’s Public Sector Development Programme (PSDP) spending in the first four months of the current fiscal year struggled at only 10 per cent of the annual allocation. Total PSDP spending in the first four months (July-October) of 2026-27 amounted to Rs103.87bn — 10.4pc of the Rs1trillion allocation, according to the Ministry of Planning and Development. Actual utilisation was far lower than the Rs412.3bn authorised by the Planning Commission. This alarming spending pattern on public-interest projects, which is affecting living standards and economic growth, has emerged despite a healthy 0.8pc budget surplus posted in the first quarter of the year. Latest data released by the Ministry of Planning and Development showed that, excluding corporations, total PSDP expenditure by about 33 ministries and divisions amounted to a meagre Rs74.65bn in the first four months, or about 11pc of the total allocation of Rs682bn. The corporations — chiefly the power sector and the National Highways Authority — together spent Rs29bn or 9.3pc against their budget allocation of Rs313bn for the whole year. Ministries, divisions utilise just Rs103.87bn in July-October against Rs1tr allocation The NHA could utilise only 5.8pc or Rs13.3bn in four months against its annual allocation of Rs225bn. The power sector was able to use Rs16bn or 18pc of its Rs98bn allocation. The Planning Commission had authorised disbursement of Rs78.6bn for NHA and Rs31bn to the power sector. Under the mechanism announced by the Ministry of Finance for the current fiscal year, the government should release 15pc of budgeted allocation in the first quarter, followed by 20pc in the second quarter, 25pc in the third quarter and the remaining in the last quarter of the fiscal year to ensure that any shortfall in revenue collection is managed through cuts in the development budget to remain with fiscal targets set with the IMF. Under this mechanism, the Planning Commission claimed that it had authorised Rs303bn for disbursement to the federal ministries in the first four months, which accounted for more than 44pc of the annual target (Rs1tr) and was higher than allowed in the finance ministry’s instructions, but only Rs75bn or 11pc, could actually be spent on the ground. Only eight ministries were able to cross the Rs1bn spending threshold in 4MFY27, led by the Water Resources Division, which spent Rs18.7bn, or 18pc of its Rs103bn annual allocation. This was followed by Rs6.88bn expenditure in Federal Education and Professional Training against its Rs36bn allocation, accounting for 19pc. Then came Rs6.6bn spending by National Health Services, Regulations and Coordination Division, achieving a healthy rate of 41pc against its allocated share of Rs16bn. As such, NHSRC exceeded the utilisation target, which was even better when seen in the context of Rs9.6bn authorisation. Next was Higher Education Commission with a funding utilisation of Rs4.7bn or 10pc of Rs46bn annual allocation. This was followed by the Ministry of Railways with Rs4.65bn utilisation, accounting for around 11pc of its Rs40.65bn allocation. The Ministry of Planning and Development itself used only Rs2.15bn, or less than 10pc, against its allocated share of Rs22.6bn. After that, the Ministry of Information Technology used only Rs1.45bn or only 7.4pc of its Rs19.6bn allocation. Combined spending in provinces and special areas (Azad Kashmir and GB) for development amounted to Rs23.8bn, or just 10pc of the annual allocation of Rs233bn and the Planning Commission’s authorisation of Rs59.8bn for the first four months. These special areas are provided funds by the finance division under a separate seasonal pattern. Likewise, despite the country being at risk of climate disasters, the climate change division spent only Rs259 million in four months or only 10.4pc of its Rs2.5bn allocation. Another critical social-sector ministry — National Food Security — utilised less than 1.5pc (Rs65m) of its allocation of Rs4.2bn. About six federal ministries could not spend even a single rupee for development in four months. They included commerce, communication, Kashmir Affairs, Gilgit-Baltistan and states and frontier regions, petroleum, privatisation, religious affairs and interfaith harmony. Published in Dawn, November 11th, 2026

items.title: Health minister denies vaccine scam allegations
items.description: • Says no public money lost in procurement controversy • Claims Rs183 million collected from applicants remains in Nadra’s account ISLAMABAD: Amid allegations of irregularities in vaccine procurement, Federal Health Minister Mustafa Kamal on Tuesday claimed that not a single rupee of public money had been lost in the controversy surrounding the procurement of vaccines for Umrah pilgrims. He said a private company had purchased the vaccines, while the entire amount collected for the purpose, amounting to Rs183 million, remained deposited in a National Database and Registration Authority (Nadra) account. Addressing a press conference, the minister said he wanted to present the facts before the nation following a week-long controversy over the vaccine procurement process. He said the health ministry would upload the inquiry report on its website to ensure transparency. It may be recalled that Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif had ordered an inquiry into the procurement of meningococcal meningitis and influenza vaccines by Border Health Services-Pakistan (BHS) under a public-private partnership (PPP) arrangement for pilgrims and overseas job seekers. It was alleged that the previous vaccination arrangement involved a cost of around Rs1,250 per dose per person, whereas the amount under the new arrangement was approximately Rs4,500 per pilgrim. The prime minister had constituted a five-member committee, headed by the secretary of the Cabinet Division, to examine the procurement process and determine whether it complied with the relevant rules and procedures. Mr Kamal explained that BHS had approached the ministry regarding vaccination requirements for people travelling abroad for Umrah. The ministry constituted a procurement committee on May 9 and also established a grievance committee, headed by the director general of health, to address complaints. However, he claimed that BHS officials subsequently formed their own committees, including procurement and appellate committees, bypassing the ministry’s arrangements and violating prescribed procedures. The minister said the inquiry found that BHS officials had bypassed the Ministry of Health and violated Public Procurement Regulatory Authority (PPRA) rules. Nadra was also brought into the process through a public-private partnership arrangement, with payments deposited into its account. He said the inquiry held BHS officials, members of the procurement committee and a subsequent director responsible for endorsing the process. He added that the ministry had implemented all the recommendations of the inquiry committee and would constitute a new procurement committee. Mr Kamal said the Prime Minister’s Office had also directed the Federal Investigation Agency (FIA) to take action, following which the officials concerned were arrested and sent to jail. Rejecting social media claims of Rs10 billion in corruption, he said the Rs183 million collected from applicants remained in Nadra’s account. Neither the government nor the company supplying the vaccines had received any payment, he added. He claimed that the government had suffered no financial loss, although the vaccine supplier had incurred losses after procuring the vaccines while the collected amount remained deposited in Nadra’s account. Published in Dawn, November 11th, 2026

items.title: Pakistan pushing for diplomacy amid global tensions
items.description: • Strength at home and effective diplomacy abroad key to confronting emerging world order, Dar tells Margalla Dialogue • University of Chicago scholar says US can’t win Iran war; claims Washington complicit in Palestinian ‘genocide’ by Israel • Urges Pakistan to capitalise on ties with both US and China, shore up its ‘middle power’ status ISLAMABAD: Calling for stronger diplomacy, dialogue and multilateral cooperation to address growing global tensions, Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar here on Tuesday stressed that Pakistan would continue to work for regional peace, while safeguarding its sovereignty and national interests. Addressing the Margalla Dialogue 2026, organised by the Islamabad Policy Research Institute (IPRI), he highlighted that the shape of the emerging world order remains uncertain. “The choices countries make during this transition will help determine whether it produces greater cooperation or deeper confrontation,” he said. “The international security architecture faces mounting pressure. Intensifying great power rivalries, protracted conflicts and erosion of arms control agreements are increasing the risks of confrontation and miscalculation,” he noted, addressing the theme of this year’s dialogue, ‘Global Order in Transition: Navigating Strategic Uncertainty’. Posing the question “how can we safeguard our security and build a more prosperous future for our people?”, Mr Dar maintained that the answer lies in “strength at home and effective diplomacy abroad”. He noted that the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement with Saudi Arabia and Turkiye, was a defensive arrangement aimed at strengthening collective security and credible deterrence, rather than targeting any particular country. Discussing Pakistan’s international partnerships, he described relations with China as a cornerstone of the country’s foreign policy, while highlighting constructive engagement with the United States and expanding cooperation with Saudi Arabia, Turkiye, Iran, Gulf countries, Europe and Central Asia. He reiterated that Pakistan sought peace but would firmly defend its sovereignty, stressing that a just settlement of the Jammu and Kashmir dispute in accordance with UN Secu­rity Council resolutions was essential for lasting peace in the region. He also warned against Indian attempts to weaponise water, adding that Pakistan would safeguard its rights under the Indus Waters Treaty. Mr Dar also classified terrorism emanating from Afghan territory as a serious security challenge, adding that Pakistan would continue protecting its people while supporting a peaceful, stable and economically integrated Afghanistan. With regard to the Middle East, the foreign minister said Pakistan’s facilitation of the Islamabad talks between the United States and Iran in April had reflected its commitment to resolving conflicts through dialogue. Other panel discussions at the event also featured noted national and international speakers. In his keynote address during a discussion on ‘Geopolitics and the Realignment of Global Power’, Prof John J. Mearsheimer, from the University of Chicago, spoke at length about the losses incurred by the US and Israel in the war against Iran, as well as the policy failures of the Trump administration. “Trump just dismissed the views of his principal advisers and he decided instead he would listen to Netanyahu and the head of Mos­sad,” he said, adding that the two men convinced the US president that attacking Iran was a good idea. “The decision to get into this war was an irrational decision… The US is in a war that it is going to lose, there is no way the US can defeat Iran,” he said. He categorically said that Israel was committing genocide in Gaza as a means to driving Palestinians from their own territory. “That is why they are treating the Palest­in­i­ans in Gaza today in the most horrendous ways… and launching pogroms against Palestinians in the (occupied) West Bank,” he said, adding that despite their brutal methods, they had failed to achieve their objective of driving the Palestinians out. He was quite clear that Israel could not have committed this genocide without US assistance, adding that Washington was complicit in this crime, providing diplomatic support to Israel and vetoing six UN Security Council resolutions designed to shut down the genocide. Talking about the contours of great power politics, he said that the world has shifted from a unipolar world into a multipolar world. “There are now three great powers in the world: the US, China and Russia,” he said, adding that the dynamics of a unipolar world were very different from the dynamics of a multipolar world. Noting that nothing is going to change in the relationship between Pakistan and India, Prof Mearsheimer said that India could not become a great power in the near future, as it is plagued by too many issues, though it could become a formidable middle power, like Japan. Pakistan, he said, needed to strive for wealth creation to become a middle power like Germany and Japan. Pakistan, he said, was in an ideal position in the multipolar world, as it has cordial ties with both the US and China, and hasn’t had to choose between the two. As long as the wars in Ukraine and the Middle East persist, the US will continue to pivot away from East Asia, he said, noting how nice Trump is to Xi Jinping because he doesn’t want to antagonise Beijing. Noted Middle East scholar Dr Vali Nasr lauded the resilience and tactics of Iran that had led to a failure of US and Israeli policies. However, he maintained that Israel had an expansionist agenda and the war between Israel and Iran was still unfinished, adding that a military alliance between India, UAE and Israel could pose a threat to Pakistan. He added that US involvement in Iran and Ukraine had led to softening its military presence against China in the Far East, and soon all­ies like Japan and South Korea too will start reconsidering their age-old reliance on the US for security. The actions and statements of President Trump have prompted demands from Iran to quit the Nuclear Non Proliferation Treaty, he said. Former US diplomat Robin Raphel noted that if Iran leaves the NPT, it could trigger exits by other countries too. Former senator Mushahid Hussain Syed said that there was a time when decisions were made in Washington regarding other countries. “But now regime change in US is due to Iran,” he mused, recalling the recent midterm elections. Published in Dawn, November 11th, 2026

items.title: US midterms: True democracy at work
items.description: By SUNNY IKHIOYA Should democracy be the rightful route to leadership? That has been the question since the time of the early philosophers. Socrates (470–399 BC), the father of Greek philosophy, argued: “Democracy must fall because it will try to tailor to everyone. The poor will want the wealth of the rich, and democracy will give it to them. Young people will want to be respected as elderly, and democracy will give it to them. Women will want to be like men, and democracy will give it to them. Foreigners will want the rights of the natives, and democracy will give it to them. Thieves and fraudsters will want important government functions, and democracy will give it to them. And at that time, when thieves and fraudsters finally democratically take authority because criminals and evildoers want power, there will be worse dictatorship than in the time of any monarchy or oligarchy.” As recently as August 12, 2026, former President Olusegun Obasanjo asked whether there was such a thing as African democracy. He concluded: “Let us not deceive ourselves, there is nothing like African democracy. We were given Western liberal democracy by our colonial masters. Western liberal democracy that we inherited pulls from monarchy, hence we can have a government and a loyal opposition, loyal to the monarchy. But when you talk about loyal opposition in an African setting — and I have gone into many African languages — opposition means enemy. That is the word.” With the recent US midterm elections, people all over the world are beginning to believe again that democracy is practicable, if done in the right manner. The United States has shown again that it remains the leading democratic nation in the world — no one comes close — despite its wobbling and fumbling. Man, by nature, is flawed, but strong structures and institutions keep him in check. Democracy says the people’s voice must decide leadership. Sometimes, out of emotion, the choices turn out badly, as we witnessed in the decision to bring in Donald Trump. But the beauty of real democracy is that the same system allows the people to correct their mistakes in subsequent electoral cycles. That is what we have just witnessed. A strong, overbearing and intimidating presidency was brought to its knees by what was assumed to be a passive opposition party. But the people had their say, and that will remain the will of the American people until the next general election. Many people, especially those of us from this part of the world, have come to see democracy as a scam — a game of the powerful elite, the military, business oligarchs and their cronies imposing their will on the people. We see elections as a do-or-die affair, with extreme religious and ethnic sentiments on full display. True democracy is real, and the US has just shown it. When it happens, it brings so much joy to the people. As one voter said: “I had to drag my daughter out yesterday and drove her to the voting centre. America is a working democracy. Not even all the money can influence suffering Americans.” Democracy was under siege all over the world. Woke culture wars were exported to other parts of the globe, breeding extremist leaders practising the politics of hate. The UN and WTO were almost rendered comatose, as nobody could rein in the raging bull in the china shop — but the great American people just did. There is a limit to how you can use power, or it will be taken away from you. That is the purpose of democracy: the wish of the people — the one that will keep them happy, healthy and prosperous. What Socrates prophesied about democracy was becoming a reality in Donald Trump’s America, but the people stood up for their country. They stood for the philosophy that all men are created equal, irrespective of ethnicity or race. They stood for togetherness, with one love for America — a country founded on the strength of diversity, one that has always stood on the side of the people. It was a big relief to the whole world, and more especially to those pivotal countries that export Western-styled democracy to other parts of the world. It shows that no matter how challenged the people of the world have become, if they stand in unity on the side of good causes, the world will make progress. Donald Trump diminished America in the eyes of the whole world, and people wondered what had happened to the country of great world leaders that pioneered global unity and borderless trade. He did a lot of damage that will take the world years to recover from. Through his policies, the Middle East lies prostrate from endless conflicts. The invincibility of the US Armed Forces was demystified, and the war with Iran became an Achilles’ heel for the Republicans’ campaign. He couldn’t even bring peace to the Ukraine-Russia war — huffing, puffing, merry-go-rounding and achieving nothing. Trump’s actions were truly embarrassing to the good people of the US, estranging traditional friends like Canada and Europe, raising unnecessary conflicts that do no good to international diplomacy, even threatening to pull the US out of NATO. And for the first time in modern history, Donald Trump took the US into a major war without the support of its traditional partners. They all repudiated the US action, and the result is the catastrophe of the Strait of Hormuz closure and the inability of the US and Israel to bring Iran to its knees. What a shame! What lessons for Nigeria and the world? It all boils down to leadership. When we say leadership is key, people scoff at us and complain about followership, harping on the general Nigerian attitude and culture. But it takes a strong leader to change all of that. Trump was a strong leader with cult-like followers who allowed him to use power negatively. Imagine if Donald Trump had used all that support for the general good of Americans and not for selective justice and vengeful retaliation against perceived enemies. Nigeria needs a strong leader — one who will work with the wishes of the people, one who will be transparent in all his dealings, one who will not see opposition as enemies but as a gauge for performance. The leader we are talking about must put the country’s interest first, before personal and family considerations. That is the kind of leader that will inspire popular followership. You need not put the security agencies, the judiciary and INEC behind you — the people will naturally gravitate towards you. True democracy is possible when leadership and structures are well instituted. The American midterms have just shown it. items.title: Agya Koo eyes collaboration with Shirley Frimpong-Manso
items.description: They are two celebrated names in Ghana’s movie industry, each having carved a formidable reputation in their respective fields. Yet, despite their towering contributions to filmmaking, veteran actor Agya Koo and acclaimed filmmaker Shirley Frimpong-Manso have never had the opportunity to work together. Now, Agya Koo is hoping that long-awaited collaboration will finally happen, revealing that Shirley is among the few prominent producers he has yet to work with. In an interview with Graphic Showbiz, the actor disclosed that the filmmaker had approached him on a few occasions, but scheduling conflicts prevented them from working together. “I have worked with almost all the big, renowned and prominent producers in the country. The only producer I haven’t worked with is my little sister, Shirley Frimpong-Manso,” he said. Despite the missed opportunities, Agya Koo remains hopeful that they will eventually work together, suggesting that a collaboration with the award-winning filmmaker would be a welcome addition to his illustrious acting career. The actor also reflected on his contribution to the growth of Ghana’s movie industry, insisting that he has not received enough recognition for his efforts, despite being honoured during the administration of former President John Agyekum Kufuor. He recalled a period when his popularity was so significant that his name featured prominently in movie titles, with productions bearing titles such as Agya Koo Part 1 and Agya Koo Part 2. He attributed much of his success to his faith in God, recalling how he prayed to become an instrument for promoting Ghanaian movies at a time when Nigerian productions dominated the local market.

items.title: At Beyond the Ballot Summit, ALTON pledges a resilient telecom network, by Okoh Aihe
items.description: Concluding her keynote on Beyond the Ballot Summit in Abuja, Prof Abigail Ogwezzy-Ndisika wrote: Generative Artificial Intelligence and Foreign Information Manipulation pose serious challenges to our republic but they are not our destiny because technology is created by humans and human institutions retain the moral authority, legal mandate and practical capacity to defend the truth. Concerning the 2027 Election, this hints at shared human responsibility to manage technology especially in this age of AI to enable it deliver instead of permitting its adulteration that can lead to unsavory results. When Ogwezzy-Ndisika presented her very pedantic paper, Beyond the Ballot: Architectural Resilience, Generative AI and Securing Electoral Integrity for Nigeria 2027 Polls, both Gbenga Adebayo, ALTON Chairman, and Seun Okinbaloye of Channels Television, were not present in the opening day. On the second day however, they had to tackle each other on how human handling of technology can guaranty fidelity of the electoral process. The nation has a point of reference that is not inspiring. Just when everybody thought the 2023 Presidential Election was on a smooth sail, and boom, came a technical glitch that rendered it difficult for information from the polling stations to be uploaded for onward transmission. A beautiful election had been blighted within seconds, raising tension across the nation. With the stubborn intrusion of Artificial Intelligence, the organizers of the Summit, IPC, CEMESO and DAI, with support from the EU Support to Democratic Governance in Nigeria (EU-SDGN), had history in mind but they were also very conscious of how to manage the entire gamut of technology, including AI, to deliver trusted election results. Hold democracy together and be able to create more human development that can impact technological growth for humanity instead of phobia for the unknown. The second day came with significant highlights. It was the Panel Session on Telecoms Accountability and Responsible Influencing: What Should Telecom operators and Influencers Do Differently in 2027? The Session featuring Adebayo of ALTON, Dan Bello and Rukayya Muhammed, two Social Media influencers, was moderated by Okinbaloye. Almost pressed beyond limits by Okinbaloye on whether the government could shut down the telecom network for whatever reason, Adebayo contributed that there were regulatory issues and cognate developments that could be responsible for such a situation but his conclusion being that the government cannot shut down the network. This I totally agreed with because no matter what you may want to accuse the Bola Tinubu government of, one thing I can say is that it is not a rogue government that may want to act irresponsibly without recourse to the law of the land. But why was that question ever necessary? Here is my little take. Elections are coming and this government does not enjoy so much trust from the people, as with other governments anyway. All kinds of things are imputed to the government although veracity is far remote. Yet it was still good for a strategic person in the telecom echo system to address such issue. What also emerged is the kind of money politicians are paying for influencers to help push their campaign materials and messages although the gathering called for caution as even Adebayo would explain that the telecom operators have no way of determining the nature of contents being pushed through their network. Such responsibility falls on social media platforms like X (formerly Twitter), Facebook and Instagram, among others. “It is important that we distinguish between the telecommunications infrastructure that carries information and the platforms that create, host, distribute and moderate content. Telecommunications operators provide the infrastructure – the pipes, if you like – that constitute the information superhighway. We provide the connectivity that enables Nigerians to communicate, access information, conduct business and participate in the digital economy,” Adebayo explained. It was gratifying therefore, when the INEC Chairman, Prof Joash Amupitan informed that for real-time response to happen, the election agency was “partnering with global social media platforms such as TikTok, Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp, YouTube, Facebook Messenger, Telegram, X (formerly Twitter), etc. “We already have an MOU with TikTok,” he said. With Adebayo up there on the platform, people were anxious to squeeze guarantees from the operators. You have to appreciate their concerns. In the period leading to the 2023 elections, some lawmakers had argued that some of their environments were so remote and therefore uncovered by any telecom network that it would be unreasonable to want to transmit election results electronically. Some even said they still use Thuraya for their means of communication. But you see, dear friend, there is no need arguing with anybody who makes exclusive claim to the absolute truth even when falsehood looks more pronounced. Adebayo was deliberate and patient in his submission as he pointed out the differences in the times. In January 2025, this administration approved a tariff review for telecom operators which has boosted their capacity for bolder investments. Since then fresh investments have gone into expanding network capacity – building new base stations, fibre layout and even strengthening the power capacity to run their operations. “The Nigerian telecommunications industry recorded capital expenditure of approximately N2.132 trillion in 2025. Operators projected capital expenditure for 2026 was approximately N1.855 trillion. Taken together, these figures represent an investment commitment of almost N4 trillion across the two years. The investment is directed at network expansion, capacity enhancement, improved coverage and resilience,” Adebayo revealed. Consequent upon the tariff review and the concomitant investment by the operators, the industry in the explanation of Adebayo, has built an extensive telecommunications footprint, with mobile networks providing connectivity across the vast majority of the country’s population. Recent report provides the following population-coverage indicators: 2G – 95.31 percent; 3G – 89.42 percent; 4G – 84.60 percent and 5G – 13.28 percent. “These figures,” he pointed out, “demonstrate the extent of the industry’s reach, particularly with 4G, which is a principal platform for mobile broadband services. It is important, however, to distinguish between population coverage and geographical coverage,” adding that “operators have established network operation centres that continuously monitor network performance.” Some contingency plans by the operators include: Network redundancy and alternative transmission routes, backup power systems at critical network locations, traffic rerouting and network optimization, additional capacity deployment at high-demand locations, and coordination between operators and relevant public institutions. Adebayo therefore pledged that for election-related activities, operators will pay particular attention to INEC offices, polling-unit clusters, collation centres, state and national collation facilities, and other critical locations. At the Beyond the Ballot Summit, participants have alerted on the beauty and the beast of AI, ALTON has pledged the readiness of members to support the elections with a resilient telecoms infrastructure; it is now the responsibilities of Nigerians to play their role and for INEC to transform the hopes of the people to reality by conducting elections that are unblemished. items.title: Intempéries: les usagers de la route appelés à la vigilance lors de leurs déplacements
items.description: Le ministère de l’Equipement, de l’Eau et des Forêts a appelé les usagers de la route à observer un ensemble de mesures de prévention afin de garantir leur sécurité, suite au bulletin d’alerte météorologique émis par la Direction générale de la météorologie qui prévoit, mercredi et jeudi, de fortes pluies orageuses accompagnées d’importantes précipitations dans plusieurs provinces du Royaume. Dans des situations météorologiques pareilles et afin d’assurer la sécurité des usagers de la route, le ministère exhorte dans un communiqué à reporter les voyages à travers les provinces concernées durant cette période, sauf en cas de force majeure, et d'éviter les déplacements pendant la nuit, mettant en garde que certains axes routiers peuvent connaitre des perturbations de la circulation en raison des fortes pluies orageuses et rafales de vent attendues. Le ministère appelle également les usagers à se préparer avant le voyage par la vérification de l’état mécanique des véhicules, à savoir la batterie, les freins, l'éclairage, la pression des pneus, le balais d’essuie-glace, le liquide lave glace, le carburant en quantité suffisante et l'état du chauffage, ainsi qu'à être vigilants surtout au niveau des sections routières susceptibles d’être submergées notamment les points bas et les traversées de la route des Oueds et Chaâbas. Il recommande aussi d'éviter de s’aventurer sur les radiers submersibles pendant les crues, de s'abstenir de l’excès de vitesse et tout dépassement ou manœuvre brusque et de respecter la distance de sécurité entre les véhicules. Metant l'accent sur la nécessité de respecter les panneaux de signalisation et de se conformer aux instructions des autorités locales et des brigades sur place relevant des directions territoriales du ministère, il invite les usagers à contacter le Centre de permanence de la Direction Générale des Routes au 05 37 71 17 17 pour plus d'information. Le ministère rappelle que le bulletin d’alerte émis par la Direction générale de la météorologie prévoit, mercredi et jeudi, des pluviométries comprises entre 80 et 110 mm au niveau des provinces de Taza, Chefchaouen, Al Hoceima, Ouezzane, Tétouan, Sidi Kacem et Taounate, et entre 50 et 80 mm au niveau des provinces de Kenitra, Essaouira, Larache, Sidi Slimane, Agadir-Ida-Ou-Tanane, Rabat, Salé et Skhirat-Témara. Des précipitations entre 30 et 50 mm sont également prévues durant la même période au niveau des provinces de Mdiq-Fnideq, Tanger-Assilah, Fahs-Anjra, Safi, El Jadida, Nouaceur, Mohammedia, Médionna, Casablanca, Berrechid, Benslimane, Fès, El Hajeb, Ifrane, Sefrou, Tiznit, Moulay Yacoub, Meknès, Khémisset, Sidi Bennour, Inezgane – Ait Melloul, Taroudant et Chtouka – Ait Baha, ainsi que de fortes rafales de vent avec chasse-poussières au niveau de plusieurs provinces du Royaume. items.title: Alumni groups cannot fix it all – 1987 year group appeals for support for Seikwa Presbyterian School
items.description: The 1987 year group of Seikwa Presbyterian School has appealed to fellow alumni and stakeholders to unite and support efforts to address mounting infrastructural challenges at their alma mater, warning that no single alumni group can resolve the situation alone. The appeal follows a visit by the year group to the school as part of activities marking its inauguration as a development-oriented association, during which members expressed concern about the deteriorating state of facilities and the difficult conditions under which teaching and learning take place. The school, located in Seikwa in the Tain District of the Bono Region, has a total enrolment of 561 pupils and students, including 419 at the Primary and Kindergarten (KG) levels, which operate a double-stream system. However, both the Primary/KG and Junior High School (JHS) sections face significant challenges, including inadequate classrooms and desks, dilapidated structures, poor sanitation facilities, abandoned buildings, and no staff common room. Speaking during an interview, Secretary of the 1987 Year Group, Raymond Ofori, said members were saddened by the condition of the school when they revisited it after several years. “Really, after so many years, when we left the four walls of this school, I’ve never entered this school. But today, when I came, actually, I was sad in a way. The environment I saw is not anything to write home about,” he said. Mr Ofori said the group had previously assumed that everything was well with the school because members regularly passed through the community without appreciating the extent of the challenges within the premises. He said the magnitude of the challenges required a collective response from all former students. “If we leave it to the individual year groups, looking at the challenges here, one year group can’t solve it. So we are inviting all group leaders and all those who have passed through the four walls. We need you,” he appealed. According to him, the vision is to establish a stronger alumni network that can mobilise substantial resources and coordinate interventions based on the school’s most pressing needs. He noted that the school had produced several individuals who had gone on to contribute to their communities and society, making it important for former students to give back to the school that helped shape their lives. Mr Ofori explained that the 1987 Year Group had previously operated largely as a welfare association, with activities centred on supporting members during bereavements and other difficult moments. However, members later recognised that their former school also needed their attention and decided to redirect some of their collective efforts towards its development. He said the inauguration was therefore intended to formally establish the group as a development partner of the school, rather than limiting its activities to welfare matters. As part of the inauguration, the group donated educational, sporting and maintenance equipment to both the Primary and JHS sections. The items included two sets of jerseys, footballs, goalkeeping gloves, whistles, two laptop computers, a television set and a lawn mower. He explained that the sporting equipment was intended to encourage physical education and sporting activities, while the laptops and television set would provide additional resources to support teaching and learning. The lawn mower, he added, would help with the maintenance of the school environment. Other activities that marked the inauguration of the year group included a dinner that involved some teachers who taught the members during their time at the school.

items.title: China hands over remains of US airmen found along WWII Hump Route
items.description: Chinese honor guards walked forward, carrying a box containing human remains. US honor guards stepped up to receive it and carefully placed an American national flag over the box. The box held eight bone fragments recovered from a glacier more than 5,000 meters above sea level. The remains, believed to belong to US airmen who went missing along the Hump Route during World War II (WWII), had lain in the mountains for more than 80 years. At the handover ceremony in Chengdu, southwest China's Sichuan Province, on Tuesday, He Jiang, director of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Archives, and US Navy Captain Colin Alexander Eliot, a forensic expert with the Defense POW/MIA Accounting Agency (DPAA), signed a document confirming the transfer, witnessed by Chinese and American representatives. The remains were recovered in areas along the Hump Route, which was established after Japanese forces occupied Myanmar in 1942, cutting off the Yunnan-Myanmar road, China's last major overland supply link to the outside world. Stretching from the state of Assam in northeastern India to Kunming in southwest China, the air corridor across the Himalayas became a vital lifeline for Allied supplies supporting China's resistance against Japanese aggression from 1942 to 1945. The route crossed snow-covered mountains, deep gorges, glaciers and tropical forests. Violent air currents, low air pressure, hail and freezing conditions posed constant risks to aircraft flying through the region. It became known as the "death route." More than 1,000 Chinese and American aircrew members lost their lives along the route. With the high mountains and glaciers making searches exceptionally difficult, many of their remains have never been recovered. The fragments handed over on Tuesday were found by a search team organized by Jianchuan Museum, a privately-run museum in Sichuan, during expeditions to the glaciers of Nyingchi in southwest China's Xizang Autonomous Region. The searchers trekked through primeval forests and waded across rushing rivers, taking care to avoid bears in the mountains and deadly hazards on the glaciers. After repeated searches, they finally located the remains. China and the United States have cooperated in searching for American military personnel missing during WWII since the 1970s. Both Chinese authorities and civilian groups have contributed to those efforts. An official with the general office of the Central Military Commission, who attended the ceremony, said the joint efforts to recover the remains of missing US servicemen were a testament to the two countries' history of fighting side by side against Japanese fascism during WWII. China has long supported the search on humanitarian grounds and is willing to continue practical cooperation with the United States in this field, the official said, adding that such efforts could contribute positively to building a constructive China-US relationship of strategic stability. "These remains bear witness to the war against fascism and carry the history of the Chinese and American peoples fighting aggression together," said Fan Jianchuan, curator of Jianchuan Museum. "They also remind us to strengthen cooperation and make new contributions to world peace." Addressing the ceremony, Eliot spoke of the shared wartime history that the remains represent. "The remains before us represent a defining historical moment when Americans, compelled by duty to defend against aggression, stood shoulder-to-shoulder with the people of China to fight that very same threat," he said. Following the ceremony, Chinese and US representatives visited the Hall of the Heroes of the Flying Tigers, which commemorates the Flying Tigers and other American servicemen who assisted China during WWII. Through wartime artifacts and other displays, the exhibition documents the history of Chinese and American cooperation against Japanese aggression. It has received more than 10 million visitors since opening over two decades ago. The airmen's identities have yet to be established. After the remains reach the United States, the DPAA will conduct DNA testing, examine historical evidence, and compare military records. Families will be notified only after identification is confirmed.

items.title: FG coming with major agric reforms to boost food production, cut inflation — ADENLE
items.description: The Federal Government (FG) has proposed sweeping reforms in the agricultural sector, including digitalisation, mechanisation and improved coordination among government agencies in the sector, to boost food production, reduce food inflation and strengthen food security. Senior Special Adviser on Agricultural Innovation to the Federal Ministry of Agriculture and Food Security, Professor Ademola Adenle, disclosed this in an interview where he outlined plans to resolve long-standing challenges in the sector. Adenle said digitalisation will help government identify genuine farmers, monitor production, ensure transparent distribution of inputs and expand farmers’ access to markets. He said the National Agricultural Growth initiative had introduced a system where agro-dealers distribute inputs to verified farmers while monitoring their output. According to him, the intervention has increased production by 30%, with wheat output rising from 420,000 tonnes to 480,000 tonnes annually. He, however, admitted that higher production alone would not bring down food prices unless institutional weaknesses and structural inefficiencies were addressed. “Previous programmes focused mainly on production and input distribution without addressing institutional capacity, food security and agro-industrialisation,” he said. Adenle called for an overhaul of the ministry’s administrative and legal structures, noting that bureaucratic bottlenecks had limited the impact of interventions. He identified poor coordination among federal, state and local governments as a major challenge, and advocated harmonised agricultural policies across the three tiers. He also proposed performance-based financing, annual key performance indicators, stronger monitoring and evaluation, data-driven decision-making, and legislation to promote accountability and transparency. On rising food prices, Adenle blamed illegal movement of produce across Nigeria’s borders and hoarding of food commodities for creating artificial scarcity. He said the Nigeria Customs Service and the Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Commission are working with security agencies to address the problem.
